Published constructions. The inspected statements in six versions of three 2026 manuscripts, arXiv:2605.19716v1-v2
(Shao, Wei, Zhang and Zhang), 2605.04526v1-v2 and 2605.04181v1-v2 (Shahmurov), supply no profile of the target class
(the literature audit LIT365, A3069; review in the accompanying artifacts; the spectral analysis comparison of
2026-11-04T07:38:12Z, A3070). The exact self-similar family of 2605.19716 has the form u = (T-t)^(gamma-1)
U(x/(T-t)^gamma) with gamma > 1; substitution gives (E) with c = gamma > 1, and the profile is axisymmetric without
swirl, so the rotation terms cancel for every omega. Its finite-energy theorem concerns an asymptotically self-similar
evolution, not the exact profile. The later version of 2605.04526 states conditional results and says that neither a
finite-time singularity nor a regularity theorem is established; 2605.04181 works in a periodic cylinder, and its
current theorem keeps persistent-regime assumptions. This compares statements with the target class only: no
construction proof is certified or refuted, the literature is not classified, and nothing here is a nonexistence
result (A3071 OPEN).

NUMERICAL (not used anywhere as evidence for a theorem): floating-point continuation of helicity-free jet systems
reached small residuals but certifies neither existence nor nonexistence of jets (A480); the proper-cone
countertests of CO28 used a numerically located zero of the tail scalar S, and their exact canonical-pressure
versions (LIT144, LIT145) are CONFIRMED at their reduced hypotheses (A553-A554).

## 10. The next most promising mathematical step

The recommended step is in the helicity-free route at omega != 0, where the problem is now a concrete statement
about the leading tail.

In brief, four statements on this route are open. Each would remove a hypothesis from a theorem of section 1, and
the first is the most concrete.
- At no point of T0 do V and S both vanish to infinite order, for a helicity-free profile in the class of Theorem 7
whose tail is smooth near T0. With Theorem 7(f) this would give U = 0 for all such profiles (A1292); target (i) of
(1) below lists what is known at such a point.
- The tail of such a profile is smooth near T0, or T0 is empty (target (ii) of (1); all-order natural derivative
bounds give smoothness, A1145, A1190). Together with the first statement this would give U = 0 for every
helicity-free profile in the class of Theorem 7, by Theorem 7(c) and (f).
- Decay implies the derivative bound DU = O(abs(y)^(1/2)) of Theorem 7 for helicity-free decaying C^2 profiles
(section 6; (3) below). With the first two statements this would give U = 0 for every such profile.
- The witnesses (W1v), (W1i), (W2) of Theorem 6 do not occur ((2) and (3) below). This alone would give U = 0 for
every helicity-free decaying C^2 profile, with no derivative bound and no tail condition (Theorem 6, A571).
None of them concerns profiles whose helicity takes both signs; for those, the C-infinity problem (R1) of section 7
remains, listed last in (3).

(1) Primary: the single remaining tail configuration. For 2/5 < c < 1/2, every omega and a decaying helicity-free
profile with U in C^2, P in C^1 and DU = O(abs(y)^(1/2)), U = 0 unless V has a point of T0 = {V = DV = 0, S = P2 = 0} in supp curl V on the unit sphere
(Theorem 7(c); LIT201, A1057). The branch k = 0 everywhere is no longer a separate case (A1021, A1049). Known at a
point w0 of T0:
- if w0 lies outside the closure of int{k = 0}, the original profile has Omega = D Omega = 0 at its preimage, and
every neighbourhood of w0 contains an open irrotational patch or infinitely many vortical components (LIT197,
A1007-A1008);
- every neighbourhood of w0 contains points with S < -eps abs(V)^2, for each eps < 1/4 (synthesis CO49(c),
A1080; from the local pressure rigidity A1006), although this does not force P2 < 0 (A1081 REFUTED that inference;
A1082 OPEN);
- the nodal premise (N) is equivalent to V0 = 0 (A1062); if it holds, some point of T0 also has grad P2 = 0 and
D^2 P2 = 0 (LIT202, A1066);
- if V0 has full angular support, small neighbourhoods of T0 carry total index at least 2 (A1083);
- the vorticity derivative DW, given at a zero of W by the pointwise conjugacy DW = DXi D Omega DXi^(-1) with the
scattering map, is nilpotent at every zero of W (synthesis CO50(a), A1106); at a point x0 of T0,
DW Ax0 = 0 and DW^T grad P2 = 0 (A1108); inside int{k = 0} a nonflat zero of V is vortical, and at a flat one x0,
DW = Ax0 tensor l with l(Ax0) = 0 (A1107);
- outside int{k = 0}, at every zero of V near which curl V != 0 is dense, P2 and S vanish to every order below
4 (spectral analysis C46, A1096); under (N), DW = 0 at every zero of V (A1109).
What does not suffice: local tails have flat zeros of V in supp curl V with k = 0 and S != 0, of every negative index
(CO49(b), A1079), and the elliptic equation behind the index count degenerates exactly where S = 0 (A1058). So the local
tail equations away from S = 0 and the index count do not exclude T0; an exclusion must use the equations where
S = 0, or global or original-profile input. The pressure equation does bite at
finite order: at a point of T0 where V is smooth and vanishes to finite order m >= 2, S has a nonzero
Taylor term of degree at most 2m and k is flat (A1139-A1140), the leading term is automatically nonzero off
Ax0 (LIT212, A1147-A1149) and k = 0 nearby; if V is smooth and of finite order at every point of T0, all three
branches of E0 close (Theorem 7(e), A1151; an individual finite-order point is not excluded, A1272; synthesis
CO52 from an answer of the second-model review, the literature audit LIT205 and LIT209-LIT214).

Two targets remain. (i) A point of T0 at which V and S both vanish to infinite order (A1152, A1292): if S has finite
order at an infinite-order zero of V, then V = 0 nearby (the literature audit LIT220 and LIT223, A1260-A1263, A1288-A1291; Theorem
7(f)), so these are the only infinite-order points left. Known:
- Under all-order bounds curl U is flat along the whole original orbit and its backward closure (A1163, A1196); every
neighbourhood has points with P2 < delta abs(V)^2 for each delta > 0 (A1207); P2 = S >= 0 at every supported common
zero of V and curl V, so the negative-sign germs of CO49(b) are not actual tails (spectral analysis C49, A1319-A1323).
- A tail that is smooth and axisymmetric about the rotation axis on a full polar cap with V = curl V = 0 at the pole
vanishes on the cap, for every 0 < c < 1/2 and every omega (the literature audit LIT228-LIT229, A1312-A1317, after the reduced forms
LIT224-LIT226, A1294-A1302).
- The tail identities without the rank relation k grad S = q S grad k admit a smooth local pair with a supported
common flat pole (LIT227, A1304-A1308, A1310; A1309 REFUTED an exclusion from these identities alone), and the full local similarity equation without the global rank relation
admits another (LIT230, A1338-A1339, A1341-A1342; A1340 REFUTED the inference of the rank relation from the local momentum
equation), so an exclusion from these local identities must use the rank relation (a
global proof may use other global information, A1368).
- The rank relation with the other first-order identities but without the Poisson equation admits a smooth common flat
point with dense vorticity (the literature audit LIT232, A1382-A1383, A1385; A1384 REFUTED a bound on the component constants from smoothness and the
rank relation), the rank relation with the Poisson equation excludes
vertical shears (A1386), and nontrivial local tails of one fixed velocity direction, or invariant along the rotation
axis, have no velocity zero (LIT233-LIT235, A1395-A1399, A1401-A1405, A1407-A1409; wording as corrected in A1459; general axial dependence
OPEN, A1406).
- The next orbit pressure coefficient p1 is nonnegative on T0 for c != 3/7 but does not give the needed sphere-mean
inequality (spectral analysis C50, A1414-A1415, A1422).
- A spherical-mean pressure bound int P2 >= delta int abs(V)^2 on small spheres, or dense vortical components S = D
abs(k)^q with one lower bound on D, excludes the point (A1336).
- If k = 0 nearby and S < 0 off the orbit, a ratio R = abs(V)^2/abs(S) outside 1 - delta < R < q/(q-1) + delta,
bounded, with rho abs(grad R) bounded, excludes it (CO56, A1369-A1372), and so does any ratio bounded above and below
with finite transverse logarithmic Dirichlet energy, with no limit at the orbit and without the Poisson equation
(the literature audit LIT236-LIT238, A1437-A1440, A1442, A1444-A1450), and so does any positive continuous function of the CO57
potential, with no bound (A1464, A1467-A1469); other ratios (unbounded, or bounded with infinite logarithmic energy)
and sign-changing S are OPEN (A1375, A1451, A1470).
- For k != 0 there is a global kinematic model with one vortical cone on which k > 0 and common flat points on its
boundary that satisfies every tail identity except the Poisson equation (synthesis CO60, CONFIRMED as a
reduced-system countermodel, A1503-A1505; section 9), so those remaining equations alone do not exclude it, and an
exclusion needs the missing Poisson relation or some other additional local or global input (A2745; A2742
REFUTED the earlier wording).
- In the k = 0 branch with S < 0, and on one vortical component of the k != 0 branch (A1561), the local tail system
near the point is equivalent to two equations (the divergence and Poisson equations) for two unknown functions on the
orbit space, of composite type, with two distinct real characteristic lines exactly where -abs(V)^2 < qS <
-k^2/abs(X)^2 (for k = 0: where abs(V)^2 > q abs(S)), so that unique continuation from the flat point cannot come from
ellipticity alone there (synthesis CO61, CONFIRMED, A1558-A1560, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts), and at regular
points the local equations force neither R = F(phi) nor R < q (synthesis CO62, CONFIRMED, A1573-A1576,
as summarized in the accompanying artifacts).
- In the k = 0 branch a normalized form abs(V)^(-2 eta) V.dx that is closed off the zeros of V is closed across
arbitrary zero sets (the literature audit LIT244, A1541-A1545), and a globally closed one forces V = 0 for c != 1/3 (LIT246,
A1552-A1556; at C^1 regularity under the classical normalized curl relation, LIT248, A1588-A1593), but the tail
equations are not known to give this closedness (A1546, A1557, A1594).
- A global pressure bound P2 <= -abs(V)^2/(2p) on all of R^3 minus 0, p = (1-c)/c, equivalently -S >= abs(V)^2/(2 - 2c),
forces V = 0 for every omega without k = 0, helicity or rank hypotheses (the literature audit LIT249,
A1602-A1605 with C^2 P2, A1622-A1624 with continuous P2), but no local common-flat consequence follows (A1608, A1625).
- Locally, at an infinitely flat zero of V, P2 - P2(x0) <= -beta abs(V)^2 with one beta > 1 on a full neighbourhood
gives V = 0 nearby (the literature audit LIT250, A1614-A1616; in the stress-only class without the divergence condition a uniform
margin is needed, A1618-A1620, and the Euler endpoint is open, A1621), and so does abs(V)^2 <= R* H with R* < 2/3 near
a common flat point, for every omega and without a k = 0 or rank premise (synthesis CO63 at omega = 0, A1609,
extended by the auditor through flat uniformly definite double-divergence-free tensors, A1610-A1611); hence a
supported common flat point with S < 0 nearby has limsup R >= 2/3 and liminf R <= 2 (A1612, A1617; R -> R0 is not
implied, A1613).
- At omega = 0, in the k = 0 branch with S < 0 off the orbit, if max R on a sequence of full circles around the point
is at most a power of the inverse radius, the source of the angular pressure equation is positive at points
arbitrarily close to the point, and if also P2 >= 0 nearby it takes both signs there and liminf R = 2 (synthesis
CO65, A1910-A1913; omega != 0 and the period condition are OPEN, A1914).
- The positive-pressure margin cannot be dropped by local arguments for stationary incompressible flows (pointwise R >
2 does not suffice in place of a fixed R* > 2): the swirl v = exp(-1/rho^2) e_theta with nonnegative pressure is
smooth, flat on its axis and has 2 < R < 4 with R -> 2 (the literature audit LIT252, A1655-A1656); it is not a similarity profile
(positive circle circulation of the residual, A1657); whether the negative-pressure margin R* < 2/3 can be dropped is
OPEN (A1658, A1697, A1706); separately, smooth bounded stationary examples with an infinitely flat axis or boundary
have R oscillating with liminf 2 and limsup 4 (positive pressure, zero helicity; the literature audit LIT253, A1689-A1690) or with
liminf 1 and limsup 2 (negative pressure; LIT255 with zero helicity, A1691-A1692, and the compact LIT254, positive
helicity near its boundary, A1693-A1695), with divergent logarithmic ratio energy: for stationary flows, two-sided
ratio bounds do not give the finite logarithmic energy used in LIT236-LIT238; these examples do not reach the negative
endpoint 2/3, and none is a profile for any c > 0 and any omega (A1696).
- With the extra acceleration bound abs((V.grad)V) <= C abs(V)^2/r near the flat point (r its distance to the point),
every fixed R* < 2 excludes the point (the literature audit LIT257, A1698-A1702), but the tail equations are not known to give that
bound (A1703).
- In the k = 0 branch a positive bounded W^{1,2} extension of the ratio to the full transverse disk excludes a flat V
across arbitrary zeros of S (the literature audit LIT259, A1748-A1754; full rank may replace k = 0, LIT260, A1756-A1758; the
extension is not derived, A1755, A1759).
- At a zero of V of finite order with continuous pressure, if P2 = 0 at the zero, S <= 0 nearby and V = 0 on
{S = 0}, then limsup R >= 1 (LIT261, A1760-A1762, A2204; these scalar premises are needed, A2203; the infinitely
flat case is not covered, A1763), and an angular-frequency bound with finite logarithmic mean excludes a flat germ (LIT262,
A1764-A1766; not derived from the tail equations, A1767).
- Globally, in the k = 0 branch, two-sided bounds r_- abs(S) <= abs(V)^2 <= r_+ abs(S) (0 < r_- <= r_+) on the whole unit sphere force V = S = 0 for
every omega (the literature audit LIT264, A1822-A1826: a global potential that is constant on the dilation-rotation orbits attains
its maximum, and Serrin's Harnack inequality applies to the weighted 1/c-Laplace equation it satisfies), at the
natural tail regularity (LIT267, A1847-A1851; with S only C^2 and comparability alone the normalized form can fail to
be W^(1,1), LIT266, A1843-A1845, A2263, by a field that does not satisfy the full tail system; the C^2 case with the tail equations
is OPEN, A1846); the rank relation on {S != 0} may replace k = 0 for c != 1/3 (LIT268, A1866-A1871),
and the profile is then zero (Theorem 7(g), LIT269, A1873-A1878); the lower bound is needed only near the common zero
set {V = S = 0}, since every boundary point of an extremal set of the potential is a common zero of V and S with
liminf R = 0 (synthesis CO67, A1950-A1954, with LIT278, A1974-A1977, for C-infinity tails; at the natural tail
regularity, with the upper bound alone in the removal estimate, A2020-A2026); but neither the rank relation nor k = 0
everywhere nor the global bounds are derived, and the local sign-changing flat-point problem is not affected (A1827,
A1852, A1872, A1879).
- Without the rank relation a nonzero helicity-free profile with the natural bounds and the global two-sided
comparison has an open spiral sector of exact irrotational flow with a noncritical contact on supp W (LIT271-LIT272,
A1904-A1908, A1915-A1918), such sectors solve the full profile equation locally (LIT273, A1920-A1923), their
complex-power germs cannot be matched in a C^2 tail (LIT274, A1933-A1937), for 1/3 < c < 1/2 no germ with
P2 + abs(V)^2/2 = 0 can be matched in a C^3 tail (LIT275, LIT277, A1956-A1959, A1967-A1972; first-order vanishing of
the rank defect does occur for omega != 0, LIT276, A1961-A1965, A1980), the reduced identities with the comparison do
not give the rank relation (LIT270, A1880-A1885), a nonzero harmonic remainder Q = P2 + abs(V)^2/2 is compatible with
exact sectors (LIT279, A1989-A1993), planar germs with any Q are excluded in a global C^4 tail with the upper
comparison (LIT280, A1995-A1998), exact nonplanar sectors with Q != 0 whose rank defect vanishes through order four
exist for 1/3 < c < 1/2 and every omega (LIT281, A2028-A2033), vanishing through order five is excluded at axial
points with the normalization and scalar homogeneities of Theorem 7(g), for every transverse Hessian, so those sectors
have rank order exactly five (LIT282-LIT284, A2049-A2053, A2055-A2060, A2093-A2097); in the isotropic case order-four
vanishing is excluded as well except at c = 5/11, omega = 0, where an exact analytic germ of rank order five exists
(LIT283, A2058-A2059), and a general sector is not excluded (A1909, A1919, A1924, A1938, A1960, A1973, A1994, A1999,
A2034, A2054, A2061, A2098).
- A real planar scalar with a uniformly elliptic trace inequality has weak unique continuation and continuation from
infinite pointwise value order (LIT263, A1804-A1810), with no Euler application (A1811); the coupled unique
continuation theorems in the literature need a coefficient estimate that the tail system is not known to give
(A1659-A1664), so the common flat case stays OPEN (A1658, A1665).
- At a point x0 where V and S vanish to infinite order, with S = 0 on the X-orbit of x0 and S < 0 off it, and with the
smooth local tail equations including the Poisson equation -Laplacian P2 = T, T = tr((DV)^2), the pressure P2 cannot
vanish on a neighbourhood, T >= 0 near x0 makes every small spherical mean of P2 about x0 negative (and T <= 0 makes
it positive), so T takes negative values arbitrarily near x0 if the means are nonnegative along a sequence of radii
and positive ones if they are nonpositive, and T cannot vanish on a neighbourhood; for omega = 0 a zero period of
abs(S)^(-eta) V.dx about the orbit forces T > 0 at points approaching x0 (spectral analysis C60, A2127-A2132). For every omega
and every c in (0, 1/2), in the same setting, T > 0 at points arbitrarily close to x0, so T <= 0 holds on no
neighbourhood of x0, and for 2/5 < c < 1/2 even abs(sym DV)^2 > (17/2) abs(W)^2 at points arbitrarily close to x0
(spectral analysis C61, A2230-A2234; the general form excludes abs(sym DV)^2 <= mu abs(W)^2 near x0 whenever
eta (4 mu + 2)^(1/2) < 1). A sharp pointwise matrix inequality in the same argument weakens this condition to
eta C(mu) < 1, with C(mu) = 1 + (2 mu)^(1/2) for mu <= 9/2 and C(mu) = (4 + 8 mu/3)^(1/2) for mu >= 9/2, so for
2/5 < c < 1/2 and every omega abs(sym DV)^2 > 12 abs(W)^2 at points arbitrarily close to x0 (the literature audit LIT294,
A2254-A2258; the matrix inequality is attained by explicit trace-free matrices, but sharpness among tail fields and
the case eta C(mu) = 1 are open, A2259). A further carrier identity from k = 0 removes the loss for mu > 9/2:
for every c in (0, 1/2) and every omega, abs(sym DV)^2 > mu abs(W)^2 at points arbitrarily close to x0 whenever
2 mu (1 - 2c)^2 < 1, so mu = 25/2 for 2/5 < c < 1/2 (spectral analysis C62, A2278-A2282); this threshold is the limit of the
pointwise method (A2283), and at omega = 0 explicit local fields with S < 0 that satisfy the local identities and the
Poisson equation, but have no common flat point, attain it (spectral analysis C63, A2321; at such points the conclusions of C61,
C62 and LIT294 do not follow from the local identities, A2323); at the endpoint 2 mu (1 - 2c)^2 = 1 the first-jet
form of the argument fails, by explicit
first-jet data (the literature audit LIT297, A2304-A2305), and the endpoint and sharpness among tail fields are open (A2284,
A2306). In the opposite direction, for every omega the bound abs(W) <= kappa abs(sym DV) + C0 abs(V) with
0 <= kappa < 2^(1/2) holds on no neighbourhood of x0, by a quasiconformal reduction on a disc transverse to the
orbit and strong unique continuation; so every neighbourhood of x0 contains points with W != 0 and
T < epsilon abs(sym DV)^2, for every epsilon > 0 (spectral analysis C64, A2347-A2350). The endpoint kappa = 2^(1/2), C0 = 0 is
the condition T >= 0, which this method does not reach (A2351). Explicit smooth fields flat at x0 that satisfy the
identities of this setting containing neither S nor P, with T >= 0 near x0 in one case and T <= 0 near x0 in the
other, show that the constant 2^(1/2) is sharp and that neither sign of T near x0 can be excluded from those
identities and the flatness of V alone: the exclusion of T <= 0 above uses S, and an exclusion of T >= 0 needs a
further premise, such as a property involving S or the pressure (spectral analysis C65, A2375-A2378, A2745). In the setting itself
V and W vanish to infinite order exactly on the
orbit segment of x0, their zeros coincide, and every other zero of V lies on an isolated orbit segment near which
abs(V) is bounded below by a power of the transverse distance, so neither of those explicit fields can be
completed to the setting with any S (spectral analysis C66, A2404-A2407); the bound abs(W) <= C abs(V) behind this argument off
the orbit is not extended to the orbit by that method (A2408). Each zero off the orbit has an exact order N and
transverse index -N, so the transverse degree of V on small circles about the orbit on which the transverse field
is nonzero grows, as the radius decreases, by the orders of the zeros crossed, and tends to infinity if zeros
accumulate at the orbit; flatness and negative indices alone do not bound it, by explicit smooth planar fields
that are not divergence free (the literature audit LIT301, A2426-A2428, A2430; A2429
REFUTED that inference). In flowbox coordinates over the unit sphere the carrier equations without S and P are
equivalent to the planar relation div(rho0 v) = (3c - 1) rho0 beta.v for the quotient field v, so abs(div v) <= C abs(v)
and those planar fields are not quotients of carriers; the relation has no universal area multiplier unless
omega = 0 or c = 1/3, and no degree bound has been established from it (the literature audit LIT302, A2437-A2443).
Divergence freedom alone bounds no degree along enclosing curves: J2 grad prod_{j=1..K}(y(x^2 + j) - 1) has K - 1
zeros of index +1 (A2453-A2454), and the bound index <= 1 at an isolated gradient zero needs the isolation that is
in question at a flat point (A2451, A2455; A2456 OPEN). On a transverse section the curl of the pulled-back velocity
contains the vorticity only through W.X, and a carrier flat at a point of a section on which abs(W.X) <= B0 abs(V)
with B0 in L^2 vanishes near that point (spectral analysis C67 for B0 in L^p, p > 2, A2463-A2467; spectral analysis C68 at L^2, A2469-A2473,
whose scalar case is Theorem 1.1 of Y. Pan and Y. Zhang, New York J. Math. 29 (2023)), and so does one on which
abs(W.X) <= (B0 + C0/abs(y)) abs(V) with B0 in L^2 and C0 finite (spectral analysis C70, A2501-A2503); so in the setting, for each
C0 >= 0, (abs(W.X)/abs(V) - C0/abs(y))_+ and (abs(W)/abs(V) - C0/abs(y))_+ lie in no L^2 on any section disc about a
point of the orbit (A2504); more strongly, the integral of abs(W.X)/(abs(V) abs(y)) over r < abs(y) < R0, divided by
log(R0/r), tends to infinity as r -> 0, and so does the same quotient for abs(W)/(abs(V) abs(y)), so neither ratio is
weak-L^2 on such a disc (the literature audit LIT338, A2831-A2833, which uses the local boundedness off the orbit that the setting
gives; for the carrier system the weak-L^2 bound alone suffices, with no hypothesis off the centre of the section,
LIT342, A2870, A2871); and a zero off the orbit with DV != 0 is a transverse saddle (A2466). The L^2
threshold is sharp for the carrier system: for every c in (0, 1/2) and every omega there are smooth local carriers,
flat exactly on one orbit, whose two section ratios lie in every L^p with 0 < p < 2 and between two positive
multiples of (log log(1/abs(y)) + 1)/abs(y) (spectral analysis C69 and its extension to every omega by a radial Volterra
correction, A2481-A2484; the literature audit LIT304, A2508-A2511), and for every positive lambda with lambda(r) -> infinity as
r -> 0 there are such carriers with both ratios at most C* + lambda(abs(y))/abs(y), C* fixed before lambda, so
C0/abs(y) above cannot be replaced by lambda(abs(y))/abs(y) (spectral analysis C71, C72, A2532-A2537). For these carriers in their
Volterra form, and for every smooth radial factor g, positive for r > 0, nondecreasing and derivative-flat with r
g' >= g, T < 0 off the orbit, so by C61 none of them completes to (F) with S < 0 off the orbit, S = 0 on it and S flat
at x0 (the literature audit LIT305, A2549-A2555); completions to (F) with another sign or zero set of S, a Poisson pressure alone,
other carriers and a global decaying profile are not excluded (A2485, A2538, A2556 OPEN). The carrier properties above
do not fix the sign of T: adding disjoint small bumps with indefinite Hessians to the stream function of the C69 carrier
gives a smooth carrier, flat exactly on the orbit, whose two section ratios again lie in every L^p with 0 < p < 2 and
have no majorant B2 + C0/abs(y) with B2 in L^2, on which T takes both signs in every neighbourhood of x0 (the literature audit LIT306,
A2580-A2586; no completion to (F) is constructed, A2587 OPEN). The same holds when the two ratios are in addition
bounded by Cstar + lambda(abs(y))/abs(y) for a prescribed positive lambda tending to infinity, however slowly, with
Cstar fixed before lambda; with bump Hessians adapted to the section metric, such a carrier also has abs(sym
DV)^2/abs(W)^2 unbounded at points approaching the orbit where W != 0, which is consistent with the necessary conditions
of C61 and C62 (the literature audit LIT307, LIT308, A2588-A2595; no completion to (F) is constructed, A2596 OPEN). With no assumption
on the sign of T: if the section one-form is f zeta with f radial, flat and comparable to abs(V), zeta.e_theta >= d > 0,
and kappa log(1/f) - Q tends to infinity, where kappa = c/(1 - c) and Q accumulates the negative part of the divergence
of the rotated form (zeta_2, -zeta_1), then there is no completion to (F) with S < 0 off the orbit and S = 0 on it, S
flat or not; this covers the carriers of C69, including its Volterra carriers with any smooth positive nondecreasing
derivative-flat factor (A2643-A2645), C71 and C72 and smaller-amplitude versions of the two bump carriers just
described (the literature audit LIT309, LIT310, A2607-A2613, A2615, A2616). The hypotheses can be weakened: a finite exit of every
section trajectory with a uniform signed cost suffices on a fixed neighbourhood, in the radial case pointwise
positivity of the angular component with the same cost limit suffices, a normalized form g(r) e_r + h(r) e_theta with
h never zero needs no rate condition, and infinite flatness can be replaced by V and S of class C2 with V = DV = 0 at
the centre (the literature audit LIT311, LIT312, A2634-A2636, A2638-A2641). The cost condition is sufficient, not necessary: for
omega = 0 an explicit carrier with a definite angular direction, flatness, finite exits and subcritical curl ratios
has exit cost -C0 log(1/r)^4 on an invariant ray, and the scalar transport equations alone exclude a completion there
(the literature audit LIT314, A2663-A2665); a full completion in the LIT311 setting needs log(1/f) + I -> infinity uniformly and
kappa log(1/f(y_n)) + I(y_n) <= C along some sequence of section points y_n -> 0, so that sigma(y_n) -> x0, with
f(y_n) the section amplitude (f(|y_n|) in the radial case) and I the signed divergence integral along the exit
(A2666). A carrier with such a completion must fail one of the earlier sufficient exclusion hypotheses, for example
through an angular component of zeta that changes sign or tends to 0 (A2614, A2617, A2618, A2637, A2642, A2646, A2667
OPEN). This does not exclude
the point: T >= 0 near x0, and T of both signs in every neighbourhood of x0, are not excluded (A2133, A2235, A2259,
A2284, A2352, A2379, A2409, A2431, A2444, A2468, A2474, A2485, A2507, A2512, A2538, A2556, A2587, A2596, A2614, A2617,
A2618, A2637, A2642, A2646, A2667 OPEN).
- A constant S on a connected open set gives V = 0 there or only simple zeros of projected index +1 (A1249-A1251;
wording as corrected in A1366); a smooth steady swirl with an infinitely flat supported axis exists locally but solves
no similarity equation (A1205-A1206).

The general nonaxisymmetric case is OPEN (A1293, A1311, A1318, A1324, A1333, A1337, A1375). Inside int{k = 0} on {S !=
0} the tail is abs(S)^eta grad f with f solving a planar elliptic equation (A1050), which degenerates where S = 0; an
argument at S = 0 that uses this structure, the global tail or the original profile is needed. Real analytic tails,
factorial or quasi-analytic natural bounds, and analytic or polynomially nonflat original vorticity exclude such zeros
(A1156, A1163-A1165, A1193, A1195).

Let Y be the set of points of int{k = 0} where curl V != 0. Points of cl(Y) outside Y with S > 0 (the set F+ of spectral analysis
C58: supported zeros of V with DV = 0, curl V = 0 and D curl V = 0, A2014) are not excluded by the pointwise profile
laws: there are local analytic solutions of the tail identities, satisfying these laws, with an arc of such points
along an orbit of X off the rotation axis, on which V and curl V have any prescribed exact finite order N >= 2 (spectral analysis
C59, LIT285, A2086-A2089; A2090 REFUTED an exclusion from those laws and finitely many vanishing jets). The next
pressure coefficient gives a further necessary condition at such a point of finite order, that 3 Hess S + (eta/S) grad
S tensor grad S be a multiple of the metric on the plane orthogonal to X (LIT286, A2107-A2110); it excludes that
family as the tail of a helicity-free profile with the natural bounds, for every omega (A2111-A2112). Local arcs that
satisfy the condition exist (LIT287, A2114-A2118; A2119 REFUTED an exclusion from this condition alone), so F+ is not
excluded (A2092, A2113, A2120 OPEN). For smooth solutions of the local tail identities with k = 0 and S != 0 on a
connected open set G (no Poisson equation needed), either V = 0 on G or every zero of V has finite exact order N >= 1,
curl V has the same order, and near each zero the common zero set is one X-orbit arc (the literature audit LIT288, by a Carleman
estimate, A2134-A2139). So for a helicity-free profile with the natural bounds whose tail is smooth near a zero p of V
in supp curl V, with k = 0 and S > 0 on a neighbourhood of p, the zero has finite order N >= 2 and satisfies the
condition of LIT286 (A2140); the premise p in supp curl V is needed, since a local solution with V = 0 and S = P2 > 0
satisfies all the local equations, including the next-scalar equations (A2173-A2174). Points with S = 0, and points of
cl(Y) without a neighbourhood on which k = 0, are not covered (A2141 OPEN). The axial members of the LIT287 family
(the arc through e3, with the exact quadratic pressure Cauchy data of LIT287) admit no C^1 next-pressure scalar, for
every N >= 2 and every omega: the fourth pressure jet has a strictly positive coefficient that produces an angular
mode at transverse degree N + 1 which no other term of the Poisson equation contains (the literature audit LIT289, A2154-A2158). So
these members cannot be the leading tail near such a supported zero of a helicity-free profile with the natural bounds
(A2159). Other fourth pressure data, the off-axis members and general positive-pressure arcs remain open (A2160 OPEN).
For omega != 0 the axial case is closed for all pressure data: at a smooth velocity zero of exact finite order
N >= 2 at a point of the rotation axis, with S > 0 and k = 0 on a neighbourhood, a C^1 next scalar forces the
transverse pressure gradient to vanish (the literature audit LIT291, A2194-A2197), and when it vanishes no C^1 next scalar exists
(LIT290, A2180-A2185), so no such zero has a C^1 next scalar (A2198). Hence a helicity-free profile with U in C^2,
P in C^1 and the natural bounds has no zero of V in supp curl V on the rotation axis in a smooth open region of the
tail where k = 0 and S > 0, for every omega != 0 (A2186, A2199; for omega = 0 every decaying profile is zero,
Theorem 2). Off the axis, at a zero of the same kind (V, S smooth near it, S > 0 and k = 0 on a neighbourhood,
exact finite order N >= 2), a C^1 next scalar forces the component of grad S orthogonal to X = Ax at the zero to be
nonzero, so grad S is not parallel to the carrier direction there (the literature audit LIT292, A2212-A2215); for a
helicity-free profile with U in C^2, P in C^1 and the natural bounds this holds at every zero of V in supp curl V
in a smooth open region of the tail where k = 0 and S > 0, c = 3/7 included through the averaged next scalar
(A2216). These two tests do not exclude the general off-axis zero: for 2/5 < c < 1/2, every omega != 0, every
N >= 2 and every point p off the rotation axis there are real-analytic local V and S > 0 satisfying k = 0, the
local tail identities and the Poisson equation, with a single common zero arc of V and curl V through p along the
X-orbit, of exact order N, with the Hessian condition of LIT286 and a nonzero transverse gradient of S on the arc,
and an analytic next scalar that satisfies both of its transport laws exactly and whose Poisson equation holds up
to a residual O(distance^(N+1)) from the arc (the literature audit LIT293, A2236-A2240). This proves only the stated
finite-order compatibility; a full next scalar, a global tail and a profile have not been constructed, and higher
compatibility and global extension are open (A2241). The next order separates two specified members of this family
(c = 9/20, abs(omega) = sqrt(65)/10, a fixed off-axis carrier, prescribed earlier pressure jets, transverse
potential starting with Re((x + iy)^n)/n): for n = 3 analytic germs with exact scalar transports have residual
O(distance^4), while for n = 4 no smooth germ with the prescribed earlier jets admits a full C^1 next scalar, whatever
its higher Cauchy data (the literature audit LIT295, A2285-A2289). The negative case extends to the whole family: for every
0 < c < 1/2, every real r, every v > 0 and every n >= 4, no C^1 next scalar exists for any smooth completion of the
prescribed aligned-gradient, fixed-phase earlier jets with unit carrier speed and S(0) = 1 (the literature audit LIT296,
A2307-A2311). The sign of the prescribed transverse pressure gradient is material: with that gradient reversed, for
every 0 < c < 1/2, every n >= 4 and one selected rotation magnitude v(c, n), exact analytic local germs with one
common zero arc of V and W of order n - 1 have a next scalar that satisfies both transport laws and the Poisson
equation up to a residual of transverse order n + 1 (the literature audit LIT298, A2353-A2357), and the same holds, with some
negative transverse gradient, for every rotation magnitude v > 0 outside an explicit set of at most one value for
each c and n (the literature audit LIT299, A2386-A2389), and for every v > 0 without exception if the nonzero transverse
gradient may have either sign (the literature audit LIT300, A2391-A2395). These statements concern only these families;
general off-axis zeros, full solvability for n = 3, a full next scalar for the reversed or either-sign gradient
and global extension are open (A2290, A2312, A2358, A2390, A2396).
Off-axis zeros with a nonzero transverse pressure gradient, points with S = 0 and boundary points of int{k = 0}
remain open (A2187, A2200, A2217, A2241, A2290, A2312, A2358, A2390, A2396 OPEN).

(ii) Tails that are not smooth: all-order natural derivative bounds give smooth tails (A1145, A1190), the
natural bounds alone give only C^(1,alpha) (A533). Excluding T0 would give U = 0 for every helicity-free
profile with DU = O(abs(y)^(1/2)), or with limsup abs(curl U) < c/1.720646 (A1235), and every omega, by
Theorem 7(c).

(2) The witnesses of Theorem 6 at the natural scope. An escaping (W1v) half-line is the lift of a vortical zero of V
(A1018), which is a nondegenerate saddle with rho = -2(1-c) (A1020, A1022), so it is not itself the obstruction.
At the scattering direction of an escaping (W2) trace V = W = 0 and S = P2 = 0, so it lies in T0 exactly
when DV = 0 there (dynamical analysis Remark (xlvii), A1125, A1127-A1129; A1126 corrects the scalar form); DV(w) is the trace-free planar matrix of the normal
and shear strain coefficients of the trace, equivalently the limit of exp(t) times the transverse gradient
of abs(U) (A1128). A densely vortical such direction lies in T0, and a nonflat one lies outside the closure
of int{k = 0} with open irrotational patches in every neighbourhood (A1131). In the helicity-free class with the
natural bounds and the C^1_loc tail convergence (A533, A538-A539), for 2/5 < c < 1/2 and a lower-window trace, DV = 0 there if V is C^2 near the
direction, at every rate: at rho = -2(1-c) by the rank identity (B59), and at a strict rate rho < -2(1-c)
because, in transverse-disc coordinates x = w + s e + u f with e the vortical approach line, the f-component
of the contact identity of Lemma W2.14 is strictly decreasing in u on the punctured disc while it vanishes at
the two extreme points of the vortical support on a short transverse segment through any vortical point near
the direction (dynamical analysis B66, A2457-A2460); the direction is
automatically supported, so for C^2 tails it is a finite-jet T0 point (dynamical analysis B59-B61, A1729-A1737,
A1798-A1799; dynamical analysis B66, A2457-A2460; the argument does not show that it is infinitely flat, A1740 OPEN). This
supersedes the C^3 threshold of B61 and the C^(2,1) threshold of B63-B64 (A2035-A2038), and the Hoelder-range
conditions of B65 (A2445-A2448) describe an empty configuration. For such a C^2 tail the flat direction lies, at
the equality rate rho = -2(1-c), in the interior of {k = 0}, as the escaping (W1v) endpoint does (A982); at a strict
rate, D^2S = D^2P2 = 0 at the direction whenever nonzero-velocity flat-vorticity contacts accumulate there (an
explicit hypothesis), and also whenever the direction is outside closure(int{k = 0}) (dynamical analysis B67, A2515-A2519; A2521
OPEN). B67 does not give DW(w) = 0 at this flat direction: its reduced local equations, without W.grad S = 0, admit
an analytic example (c = 3/7, omega = 0) with DW(w) != 0 at a supported regular zero of S, which fails W.grad S = 0
(A2623-A2625); with W.grad S = 0 added, at a zero with V = DV = S = 0, grad S != 0 and X.V = 0 nearby, the
quadratic velocity jet has one free coefficient, DW(w) grad S(w) = 0, and DW(w) = 0 if and only if D^2V(w) = 0
(A2627, A2628); whether DW(w) = 0 for actual tails is OPEN (A2565, A2606, A2626, A2629). The natural bounds give
only V in C^(1,alpha)
(A538); without C^2 near the direction whether DV = 0 there is OPEN (A1132, A2462). At a supported nonflat (W2) direction at the equality rate rho = -2(1-c)
(grad S(w) != 0), under the hypotheses of dynamical analysis B56, the vortical components
nearby have k != 0 and S = D_C abs(k)^q with abs(D_C) -> infinity along every vortical approach, so infinitely many
components accumulate there (dynamical analysis B58, A1423-A1426, A1455; A1427 REFUTED a finite-time power law; A1428 OPEN); if V
is C^2 near the direction this case does not occur (B59).

(3) In parallel: the witnesses of Theorem 6 (owner dynamical analysis), whose exclusion would remove the tail hypotheses at C^2
for helicity-free profiles; the derivative-decay question of section 6, whose positive answer would make Theorem 7
apply to every helicity-free decaying profile (integral-estimate analysis, target (T-H3), with the written obstruction of A682-A688 (A689 OPEN for method completeness); under
polynomial Holder growth of curl U, a bound of the backward-segment misalignment average of the vorticity by
1 + c/2 - epsilon suffices, A904; neither condition is derived from decay, A909, A946); and
the sign-changing basin of (R1), which is the C-infinity problem without any helicity condition.

What is known not to work, so not worth repeating: scalar identities that hold for reduced models with an
independent pressure (section 7, (R1)); arguments that use only the kinematic identities, which the models of
section 9 satisfy; weights alone at a zero of V (the Dirac mass at a zero is invariant); and the specific integral
quantities listed in Appendix B.10.

(d) If V is of class C3 and P of class C4, the bound P >= gamma abs(V)^2 on B forces V = P = 0 for every such pair if and only if gamma > gamma_smooth = max(1/6, Gamma_2): for every gamma <= gamma_smooth some nonzero polynomial pair satisfies the bound (LIT318, A2700). Since Gamma_2 < 5/32 < 1/6, gamma_smooth = 1/6 (LIT336, A2822; earlier gamma = 2499/10000 was shown to suffice, LIT320, A2706): every gamma > 1/6 forces V = P = 0, while the swirl V = rho^2(-y, x, 0) with P = rho^6/6 = abs(V)^2/6 satisfies the bound at gamma = 1/6. So at this regularity the threshold is exactly 1/6, below the value 1/4 that is sharp at C2 velocity and C1 pressure (LIT315, preceding row). (e) Fix 0 < alpha <= 1. If V is of class C2 with abs(D2V(x) - D2V(0)) <= C abs(x)^alpha near 0 and P is of class C1, the bound P >= gamma abs(V)^2 on the whole ball B with gamma > max(Gamma_2, 1/(4 + 2 alpha)) forces V = P = 0 (LIT323, A2736); the proof uses a homogeneous quartic limit of the rescaled pressures, which exists along subsequences without C4 regularity (A2735). For every gamma <= max(Gamma_2, 1/(4 + 2 alpha)) a nonzero pair with locally C^(2,alpha) velocity satisfies the bound: the swirl V = rho^(1 + alpha)(-y, x, 0) with P = rho^(4 + 2 alpha)/(4 + 2 alpha), for which P = abs(V)^2/(4 + 2 alpha), or the attained pair of (c) (A2737). Since Gamma_2 < 5/32 < 1/(4 + 2 alpha), this threshold equals 1/(4 + 2 alpha) for every 0 < alpha <= 1 (LIT336, A2823). At alpha = 1 it is 1/6 under a Lipschitz bound on D2V at the centre and C1 pressure, so (e) contains the vanishing half of (d). As alpha -> 0 the threshold 1/(4 + 2 alpha) tends to 1/4, and it is below 1/4 for every alpha in (0, 1]. (f) For a nonzero divergence-free homogeneous quadratic Q and real gamma, let C_gamma be the symmetric matrix with x.C_gamma x = -tr((DQ(x))^2) - gamma Delta(abs(Q)^2)(x), and let lambda_1, lambda_2, lambda_3 be its eigenvalues. A homogeneous quartic R with -Delta R = tr((DQ)^2) and R >= gamma abs(Q)^2 exists if and only if lambda_1 b_1 + lambda_2 b_2 + lambda_3 b_3 >= 0 for all b_i > 0 with b_1 + b_2 + b_3 = 1 and 1/b_1 + 1/b_2 + 1/b_3 <= 49 (LIT331, A2790, A2791). If C_gamma is not a multiple of the identity, the least value m of the left side over these b is Z_+/Z_- - mu, attained only at b_i = 1/[Z_- (lambda_i + mu)^(1/2)], where mu > -min lambda_i is the unique root of Z_+ Z_- = 49 with Z_+ = sum_i (lambda_i + mu)^(1/2) and Z_- = sum_i (lambda_i + mu)^(-1/2); for C_gamma = lambda I it is lambda (LIT332, A2794). In the first case, with nu = 1/Z_-^2 and the symmetric matrix A = Z_- (C_gamma + mu I)^(1/2) - 7I, the quartic F = (nu/8)(x.Ax)^2 + (m/20) abs(x)^4 has Delta F = x.C_gamma x and is nonnegative exactly when m >= 0, so R = gamma abs(Q)^2 + F is an explicit admissible quartic whenever the test holds (LIT333, A2806). If B > 0 with tr(B) = 1 and tr(B^-1) = 49, the only nonnegative homogeneous quartics F with Delta F = x.Cx and tr(BC) = 0 are kappa (x.(B^-1 - 7I)x)^2 with kappa >= 0; so every nonzero matrix on the boundary of the cone has exactly one nonnegative preimage, and the sum of two nonzero members of the cone on different rays lies in its interior. Consequently, for each Q for which some gamma admits such an R, the largest such gamma, gamma_Q, is attained by exactly one R, which is gamma_Q abs(Q)^2 or gamma_Q abs(Q)^2 + kappa (x.(B^-1 - 7I)x)^2 for such a B and some kappa > 0 (LIT335, A2812-A2814). The proof identifies the Laplacians of the nonnegative ternary quartics as a closed cone with dual {0} union {B positive definite: tr(B) tr(B^-1) <= 49}, using Hilbert's theorem that every nonnegative ternary quartic is a sum of squares of quadratic forms (LIT331). A second proof avoids Hilbert's theorem and cone separation: every C in the cone is the Laplacian of a sum of at most two squares of quadratic forms, and for each nonzero B in the dual the functional F -> tr(BC), where Delta F = x.Cx, is a nonnegative combination of at most 24 point evaluations of F, or 12 after antipodal pairing (LIT334, A2805). For the fixed field z(-y, x, 0) the test gives exactly gamma <= (6 - sqrt30)/24, as in (c) (A2792). This is an exact test for each Q; it does not evaluate Gamma_2 (A2793, A2795, A2807, A2815). A bounded floating-point search over all divergence-free quadratics with this test, 724 local optimizer runs over gamma in [0, 0.251], found no gamma above g_star (NUMERICAL, record audited A2808); it gives no upper bound for Gamma_2. The quadratic example pairs displayed in (b) and (c) are not stationary Euler fields and are not rotating similarity profiles for any c > 0 and any omega (A2696, A2703, A2709, A2719). The non-Dini pair of (a), the cubic swirl V = rho^2(-y, x, 0) with P = rho^6/6, one of the sharpness pairs of (d) at gamma = 1/6, and the swirls of (e), which give the cubic swirl at alpha = 1, are stationary Euler fields (A2693, A2700, A2737); the swirls of (e) have similarity residual [1 + c(1 + alpha)]V for every omega, nonzero for c > 0, and grow at infinity (A2737). The attained pair of (c) is a nonzero homogeneous quadratic, so it does not decay, and with its quartic pressure it is not a similarity profile for any c > 0 and any omega (A2737). (d) The threshold is sharp: for every omega^2 > 2 and every real c the linear field U = Mx with M = [[1, omega, 0], [omega, -1/2, -w/2], [0, w/2, -1/2]] and P = x.Hx/2, H = [[omega^2 - 2, -3 omega, 0], [-3 omega, K - 3 omega^2, 0], [0, 0, K]], K = (1 + w^2)/4, solves the profile equation on R3, and H is positive definite exactly when K > 3 omega^2 + 9 omega^2/(omega^2 - 2); these fields grow linearly and do not decay (A2749, A2754). (f) Let U(0) = 0 and W != 0, and write e = W/abs(W), u = omega^2 abs(Je)^2, v = omega e.e3, a = u - 2, tau = u(3u + 3 + v^2)/a, R = abs(h) with h = ((3u + 9u/a - uv^2/a)/2, 3uv/a), and K_min = tau/2 + R - v^2 if R >= 2v^2, K_min = tau/2 + R^2/(4v^2) otherwise. If the Hessian of P at 0 is positive semidefinite, then u > 2 and abs(W)^2 >= 4 K_min - 1. Conversely every (omega, W) with u > 2 and abs(W)^2 >= 4 K_min - 1 is the central data of a linear profile on R3, for every real c, with positive semidefinite pressure Hessian, positive definite exactly when abs(W)^2 > 4 K_min - 1; at equality every positive semidefinite Hessian is singular (A2760, A2761). (g) For every real c and omega, U(0) = 0, W != 0 and a positive semidefinite Hessian of P at 0 give abs(W)^2 >= 59 + 24 sqrt(6), strictly if the Hessian is positive definite, and with U(0) = 0 a positive definite Hessian forces W != 0; the constant is attained by a linear profile with positive semidefinite Hessian, for example at omega^2 = 2 + sqrt(6), and approached by linear profiles with positive definite Hessian (A2764, A2765); with u and v as in (f), it is attained exactly when u = 2 + sqrt(6) + beta v^2 and 0 <= v^2 <= z_star, where beta = (sqrt(6) - 2)/3, z_star = (a_star - sqrt(6))/beta and a_star = (12 + 6 sqrt(6) + 4 sqrt(27 + 11 sqrt(6)))/(8 + 3 sqrt(6)), so for 2 + sqrt(6) <= omega^2 <= 2 + sqrt(6) + (1 + beta) z_star, about 13.69 (A2803).
