## Appendix B. Detailed results by topic

This appendix is the chronological working record behind sections 1 and 4-10, retained with presentation edits: item 1 of the earlier record (items 1a-1e) as B.1 and its sections 4-10 as B.4-B.10. Its statements and status labels are historical. Where a later entry, a theorem of section 1 or a later auditor verdict supersedes a statement or an OPEN or SUBMITTED label, the later text is the current one, and an earlier literal statement should not be quoted on its own (A1281). Each entry carries only the scope of the verdicts it cites; the auditor's check of the assembled report covers the front matter, sections 0-10 and Appendix A, and treats this appendix as a record. References within this appendix such as "item 1d" or "section 6" refer to these subsections.

### B.1 Results by topic (historical item 1, items 1a-1e)

1a. Energy law (integral-estimate analysis Theorem A; PROVED, A040, A052-A054). Bounded C^1 profile with distributionally vanishing
dilates, any omega. 0 < c < 2/5: U = 0. c = 2/5: U in L^2, tail O(R^-5). 2/5 < c < 1: E(R) = L R^(5-2/c) + O(R^(4-2/c)),
L > 0 unless U = 0. The c < 2/5 part is not new: it is Chae-Shvydkoy
Theorem 3.2 with p = infinity and, in rotating form, Chae-Tsai Theorem 3.2 (section 2.9; the literal bounded endpoint
p = infinity, alpha = 0 of both theorems, outside the range used here, fails for nonzero constants, A1481-A1485, A1768-A1770); the proof here is independent.
The dilation hypothesis can be removed (Corollary A.5; PROVED, A406-A407): every bounded C^1 profile has a unique
constant background b, the weak-star limit of U(R.), and U(. + z0) - b with z0 = -(cI - omega J)^{-1} b is again a
profile and satisfies the hypothesis. So for 0 < c < 2/5 every bounded C^1 profile is constant (with
P = -((1-c)b + omega J b).y + constant), and in 2/5 <= c < 1 the energy law holds for U - b after this shift.

1b. Structure theorem for a hypothetical nonzero profile in 2/5 < c < 1/2, every omega (all parts PROVED unless
marked): E(R) = L R^(5-2/c) + O(R^(4-2/c)) with L > 0 (A052); not axisymmetric about the rotation axis (A010 after the cancellation of the rotation terms used in A046); infinite-volume vortical
set (A067), positive density in every shell at infinity (CO7, A092); a positive-measure vortical set whose
backward limits are not points or single cycles (A020, A011, A058); trichotomy of those limits (A056), refined by CO9 (A115): up to a null set, case (alpha) is the union of the basins
of countably many regular basic hyperbolic backward attractors, each with h_top = 1-2c and a physical measure of
maximal entropy (A085), each basin a union of complete vortex lines through the attractor; limit sets made of
vortical equilibria occur only on a null set (A111), and so do limit sets contained in {B = 0}, including those meeting
irrotational zeros (A122); every
compactly supported ergodic B-invariant probability measure giving full mass to {B != 0, Omega != 0} has
Lyapunov spectrum {1+c, 0, 2c-1} with Omega the strong direction (A037; this says nothing about the spectrum at
stagnation points or of measures carried by irrotational points, and other equilibrium spectra occur, A095); h_top >= 1-2c on Lambda for C^infinity
profiles (A055) or C^2 profiles with Omega nowhere zero on Lambda (A080); zero total helicity under a natural
annular L^2 vorticity bound (CONDITIONAL, A083); for omega != 0 the only C^1 functions of
(y, U, DU, P) whose formal derivative along B is nonpositive at every admissible formal second jet are constants,
while for omega = 0 they are exactly the nondecreasing functions of H_0 = H - c(1-2c)abs(y)^2/2 (A081, A2178;
A2177 REFUTED the same statement with the unshifted H; the unqualified
phrase "no first-order Lyapunov function" is false at omega = 0, A167; inequalities that use global properties of
decaying profiles are not covered); a zero of B that is the backward limit of a
nonstationary orbit of a compact invariant set in {Omega != 0} has real spectrum {1+c, lambda_2, lambda_3} with
lambda_3 < 0 <= lambda_2 (B19, A147).

1c. Smooth vortical basin coverage and the helicity-sign Liouville theorem (coverage PROVED in the C-infinity class, and
the Liouville theorem CONDITIONAL on the helicity sign there; the literature audit LIT41
and LIT65-LIT67, the auditor; A305-A309. The finite-regularity versions are CONDITIONAL: on a strain bound, A312 and A373,
or on Gamma_Z < r(1-2c), A416-A417 and A422, or on the weaker componentwise bounds
Gamma_E < r(1-2c), A430-A432).
(i) Coverage (A308). For every nonconstant C-infinity uniformly sublinear profile, every 0 < c < 1/2 and every omega,
almost every point of {Omega != 0} lies in the continuous-time basin of one of countably many compactly supported
SRB probabilities of the backward carrier. Each is ergodic for the whole flow, gives full mass to
{B != 0, Omega != 0}, has exponents (1-2c, 0, -(1+c)) and entropy 1-2c, and has absolutely continuous unstable
conditionals. The finite-time curve construction is elementary (A305-A307); no unaudited source is used. The supports
may meet {B = 0} or {Omega = 0}, so this is not coverage by regular attractors. With A207 and A223 the basins have
pairwise disjoint invariant open essential domains D_nu that cover {Omega != 0} up to a null set.
(ii) Liouville theorem (A309). Let the profile be C-infinity and decaying, 2/5 <= c < 1/2, omega arbitrary. If
U.Omega has one sign on each D_nu (the sign may depend on nu), then U = 0. In particular a smooth decaying profile
whose helicity density U.curl U is everywhere >= 0, or everywhere <= 0, vanishes. Equivalently, a nonzero smooth
decaying profile has an essential basin on which U.Omega takes both signs on nonempty open sets. No Dini condition,
finite energy, symmetry or mixing is assumed.
Part (i) also holds, CONDITIONAL on a strain bound, for C^r profiles, r >= 3, under the quantitative condition (r-1)(1-2c) > L_+ + L_-, where L_+ and
L_- are the largest expansion and contraction rates of the symmetric part of D(-rho(cy + U)) for a radial cutoff rho
(A373; this sharpens the condition (r-1)(1-2c) > 3L of A312, LIT68). Since L_+ + L_- >= 2-c for every nonconstant
profile, the condition requires r >= 10 at c = 2/5 and r >= 17 at c = 0.45. The equivalence in (ii) is checked in
A317 at the C-infinity scope and at the finite-r scope of A312; A317 predates the sharper condition of A373. Part (i) also holds for C^r profiles, for every integer r >= 2, under a growth condition on degenerate measures
(CONDITIONAL on that condition, a hypothesis of type H6). In its global form (A398-A399, A416-A417) every ergodic
invariant probability carried by {B = 0} or {Omega = 0} in the absorbing core K of the backward flow has largest
Lyapunov exponent below r(1-2c); equivalently, when Omega is not identically zero, r(1-2c) > Lambda_core, the
exponential growth rate of the derivative of the backward flow on an absorbing ball Q, and then Lambda_core >= 1-2c
(A398-A399 assume Omega is not identically zero; for U = 0, Lambda_core = 0 while max(1-2c, Gamma_Z) = 1-2c, A484;
coverage is vacuous when Omega is identically zero). In its componentwise form (the literature audit LIT89;
A430-A431), which is weaker, the condition is imposed separately on each connected component E of {Omega != 0}:
Gamma_E < r(1-2c), where Gamma_E is the largest exponent of ergodic probabilities on
Z_E = K cap closure(E) cap ({B = 0} cup {Omega = 0}), attained when Z_E is nonempty (Gamma_E = -infinity if Z_E is
empty; A430, A481, A484); equivalently Lambda_E < r(1-2c), where Lambda_E = max(1-2c, Gamma_E)
is the growth rate of the derivative on Q cap closure(E) (A430). No gap uniform over components is needed, and
probabilities in the interior of {Omega = 0} or outside every component closure do not enter. At C^2 the condition is
Gamma_E < 2(1-2c) for every E. It includes point masses and measures of entropy zero. Whether decay implies it at
r = 2 is open (A456). A sufficient pointwise form is lambda_min(sym DU) > -(c + r(1-2c)) on each compact Z_E, because
every compact ergodic carrier probability nu has largest backward exponent at most -c + int (-lambda_min(sym DU)) dnu
(spectral analysis C32; A454, CONFIRMED); decay is not known to give this strain bound either. No local identity implies it: exact affine (nondecaying) profiles have a vortical equilibrium whose
exponent is arbitrarily large, for every omega (A415), and exact local profiles have an irrotational periodic carrier
orbit with arbitrarily large exponent, for every omega != 0 (A423; cubic growth or a singularity at the origin). For a
nonstationary ergodic probability on {Omega = 0} on which D Omega is not almost everywhere zero, the largest exponent
is exactly (1-2c)/2 or exactly 1+c (A433, from the literature audit LIT90, local C^2); since 1+c > 2(1-2c) for c > 1/5, the second
case is not excluded by the C^2 test, and probabilities on which D Omega = 0 and carrier equilibria are not restricted.
In the global helicity-free class (U.Omega = 0 everywhere, U in C^2, uniformly sublinear) the 1+c case is narrowed
further (the auditor A442, A444, A445, A449): on such a probability U.B = 0 and H is constant on the support, and the
velocity is transported as a covector with rate -(1+c) or 1+4c; the rate 1+4c forces a single periodic orbit and is
excluded, and a periodic orbit with rate -(1+c) is excluded as well. For a measure that is not excluded, one regular
component of the Bernoulli level {H = h} carries full mass; it is noncompact, and the rest of the support lies in
{B = 0} cup {D Omega = 0} (A458, from the literature audit LIT95). The support must contain a zero of B (A460, LIT100); at a
zero p != 0 the spectrum of DB(p) is (-(1+c), lambda, 1+4c-lambda) with lambda <= 0, and lambda = 0 if D Omega(p) != 0
(A461, LIT101); U has no zero on the support (A464, LIT103), and a measure whose support contains no zero of U is
periodic (A465-A466, the literature audit LIT104), hence excluded by A449. So in this class no such measure exists, and every
compact ergodic probability with B != 0 and Omega = 0 almost everywhere either has D Omega = 0 almost everywhere or has
backward spectrum ((1-2c)/2, 0, -3c-(1-2c)/2), whose top exponent is below 2(1-2c) (A467). Such a probability that is flat (B != 0 and D Omega = 0 almost everywhere; carrier equilibrium atoms are the separate
case below, A490) whose support lies in closure{Omega != 0}, which is automatic for probabilities on Z_E (A484), has U.B = 0 on its support (A470,
The literature audit LIT106), a constant covector rate rho and backward spectrum (0, -rho, rho - 3c), and it is periodic unless its
top exponent is 0 (A471, LIT105). Hence in this class, for each component E of {Omega != 0}, Gamma_E >= 2(1-2c) can be
witnessed only by a carrier equilibrium atom or by a flat periodic orbit with rho <= -2(1-2c) or rho >= 2 - c, and for
decaying profiles with 2/5 <= c < 1/2 the exclusion of both witness types would give U = 0 (A432, A471). A vortical
carrier equilibrium p is nonzero and has spec DB(p) = (rho, 1+c, -(1-2c) - rho) with rho real; its top backward
exponent is below 2(1-2c) exactly when -2(1-2c) < rho < 1-2c (A468). A469 gives two spectral families at nonzero
irrotational equilibria with D Omega != 0. At an origin with U = Omega = 0, D Omega(0) = 0, and DU(0) != 0 if the
origin lies in closure{Omega != 0} (A472, LIT102). More strongly, a carrier equilibrium with U = 0 (in particular
the origin) has an irrotational neighbourhood in this class, so every carrier-equilibrium witness is a point p != 0
with U(p) != 0 (A478, synthesis CO26; local: rank identity, Cauchy law and zero helicity near the point suffice).
Every vortical carrier equilibrium in this class has rho <= -(1-2c), for every omega and with no decay hypothesis
(A496, CONFIRMED; synthesis the second-model review with check as summarized in the accompanying artifacts and an independent auditor
proof; it uses A413, A468 and A478). So the vortical equilibrium witness has rho <= -2(1-2c); the upper range is
excluded. In the lower range, with no decay or derivative bound: if the connected component L_p of
{H = H(p)} through a vortical carrier equilibrium p is compact, then rho = -(1-2c), so rho < -(1-2c) forces L_p to
be unbounded; and every point q with f(q) != 0 (f = (B x Omega).grad H/|grad H|^2) on the regular level component
through p, which exist arbitrarily close to p, either escapes forward or has a compact hyperbolic limit set in
Crit(H), Crit(U.B) and L_p whose vortex saturation is unbounded (A508, A510, CONFIRMED; the auditor synthesis with
reviews by spectral analysis and the synthesis, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts). A nonempty compact B-invariant subset of
Crit(H) with B x Omega != 0 always has unbounded vortex saturation, and for omega = 0 it cannot exist, since
B|y|^2 = (2/c)|B|^2 on {U.B = 0}; so for omega = 0 every such q escapes (A511, CONFIRMED; synthesis check
as summarized in the accompanying artifacts of the second-model review). With U -> 0, DU = O(r^(1/2)) and 1/3 < c < 1/2, the
far-field tails of A498 give a common limit H_inf of H and P, and a lower-range witness has H(p) = H_inf (A508); with
V, Omega_* the A210 tails and E = -(1-2c)V + Ay x Omega_*, grad H = E + o(r^(1-1/c)), E has a zero on S^2, and every
escaping or saturating limit direction lies in the zero set Z_E (A509, spectral analysis C35); a limit direction that is a
connected component of Z_E is also a common zero of V and Aw x Omega_* (A512, spectral analysis C36; such singleton components
remain possible at common zeros, A515). Escaping points are open and dense in the part of the regular level through p
where f != 0, for every omega and with no decay or derivative bound (A517, CONFIRMED; spectral analysis C36 Lemma 10). With U -> 0
and DU = O(r^(1/2)), for 2/5 < c < 1/2, grad P = O(r^(1-2/c)), P - H_inf = O(r^(2-2/c)) and U - V = O(r^(1-2/c))
(A516, CONFIRMED; spectral analysis C36 Lemma 9, the literature audit LIT131 and the auditor, no helicity condition used), and every lower-range
witness yields a regular C^1 arc of Z_E along which Y(w) = Omega_*(w) - (w.Omega_*(w)/c)Aw != 0 and (1-2c)V(w) = Aw x
Omega_*(w) != 0 (A518, CONFIRMED; spectral analysis C36 Theorem 11). The nonzero limiting velocity on an escaping orbit of the
level gives abs(grad H) >= c_0 e^{(rho-c)t} along it, while A516 gives O(e^{-(2-c)t}) for grad(H - U.B) = -(mu/(1-2c))
grad H there; hence in 2/5 < c < 1/2 every vortical carrier equilibrium has rho = -(1-2c) or rho <= -2(1-c), for every
omega (A518; the synthesis check as summarized in the accompanying artifacts of the second-model review reaches the same bound
independently). The lower range is excluded whenever Z_E is totally disconnected or Y = 0 on Z_E (A518), conditions
not derived from the equation; an exact homogeneous tail with E = 0 identically (A514, spectral analysis C35 Remark 7; singular at
the origin and not a profile) shows that the kinematic tail identities alone allow Z_E = S^2. This explicit tail
cannot be the leading tail of a helicity-free target profile: no such profile with U -> 0 and DU = O(r^(1/2)) has
U = sigma V_b + o(r^(-p)) with sigma != 0 and V_b the A514 tail, for any omega, with smaller corrections and no
symmetry of the profile assumed (A532, CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT130, LIT133 and an auditor proposal). The tail inputs are
CONFIRMED without any helicity condition, for 2/5 < c < 1/2, every omega, U -> 0 and DU = O(r^(1/2)) (p = 1/c - 1):
P - P_inf = P_2 + o(r^(-2p)) and grad P = grad P_2 + o(r^(-2p-1)) uniformly, P_2 the canonical pressure of V (A530);
the rescaled velocities converge in C^(1,alpha)_loc off the origin for every alpha < 1, and for bounded U the escape
limit map is onto R^3 minus 0 (A533, spectral analysis C37 Lemma 16); under the natural bounds |U| <= C(1+r)^(-p),
|DU| <= C(1+r)^(-p-1) the rescaled velocities are also uniformly bounded in W^(2,q)_loc off the origin for every
finite q > 3 (A538, the literature audit LIT136, no helicity condition; no C^2 convergence is claimed); the first twisted correction converges weak-star to
DV V + grad P_2, and with global zero helicity S = P_2 - abs(V)^2/2 is constant along every C^1 integral curve of
curl V (A531, the literature audit LIT134); H - P_inf = k + R + o(r^(-2p)) uniformly with k = (Ay).V and R = V.grad k - (1-2c)S
(A535). On the limiting sheet of an escaping regular level of a vortical carrier equilibrium in the lower range,
S = 0; at the endpoint rho = -2(1-c) (mu = -(1-2c) - rho = 1), grad S = -V/f_0 != 0 and k = 0, E = grad k = 0 on an
open twisted cone around the sheet; for rho < -2(1-c) (mu > 1), grad S = 0 on the sheet (A534, CONFIRMED with global
zero helicity; spectral analysis C37 Proposition 17 and Theorem 18; this replaces an earlier synthesis statement that was
conditional on a localized Chae-Wolf theorem). The cone need not be all of R^3 minus 0, and no endpoint or strict
lower-range witness is excluded. The next tail term also converges: p_t -> P_2 in C^(2,alpha)_loc, S_t -> S in
C^(1,alpha)_loc, exp(t)(u_t - V) -> DV V + grad P_2 in C^alpha_loc, and along each escaping carrier orbit
exp(t)(G(t) - E(v)) -> DV(v)^T E(v) - (1-2c) grad S(v) (A539, CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT138; no helicity needed for the
convergence). With E = 0 on all of R^3 minus 0 the degenerate tail is excluded in two classes: if every zero of S has a
C^1 nodal chart of order m and codimension k = 1 or 2 with m beta < k, beta = (1-2c)/(2(1-c)), then V = 0 (A547,
CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT137, LIT139, LIT142; an exact singular kinematic countertest at omega = 0 with m beta = 2 shows
that the kinematic identities alone do not reach the threshold, A548); and an axisymmetric tail with the actual
pressure Poisson equation vanishes for omega != 0, while at omega = 0 a nonzero residual must be one-signed and purely
azimuthal, so a target helicity-free profile whose leading tail is axisymmetric with E = 0 globally is zero for every
omega (A549, CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT141). Both need E = 0 globally. The proper-cone countertests (synthesis CO28, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts, with a NUMERICAL zero of S; their exact canonical-pressure versions the literature audit LIT144 and LIT145, A553 and A554, CONFIRMED at their reduced hypotheses) show that kinematics, the canonical Poisson equation, W.grad S = 0 and the A534 sheet conditions do not by themselves give global E = 0, for every omega; but they omit the confirmed tail rank condition grad k x grad S = 0 on {curl V != 0}, which forbids their poloidal plateau from ending (A555, CONFIRMED), so they violate it. With the rank condition kept, an axisymmetric C^1 homogeneous tail with the actual Poisson pressure has no point with S = 0, grad S != 0 and curl V != 0 for 1/3 < c < 1/2 and every omega; hence a target globally helicity-free profile with natural bounds whose actual leading tail is axisymmetric has no mu = 1 escaping-sheet endpoint (A556, CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT146; neither global E = 0 nor symmetry of the profile is assumed; the synthesis statement that the step needs profile input beyond the leading tail is withdrawn). For the same class the conclusion extends to every lower escaping rate: a C^1 axisymmetric homogeneous tail with actual Poisson pressure, zero helicity, curl V.grad S = 0 and the rank condition is either 0 or pure swirl with angular amplitude F of one strict sign and S = C r^(-2p) abs(F)^(2p/(p-1)), C < 0 (A561, CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT147; a necessary class, neither constructed nor excluded there); E = grad k = 0, S = 0, V != 0 is then impossible for every omega, so a target globally helicity-free profile with natural bounds whose actual leading velocity tail is axisymmetric has rho = -(1-2c) at every vortical carrier equilibrium and lambda = 1 on every A536 regular vortical zero-g component, and the same holds for the effective rho in the nearby-vortical-level irrotational case of A537 (A562, CONFIRMED as a conditional exclusion; separating irrotational levels, flat witnesses and nonaxisymmetric tails are not covered). The literature audit LIT150 (CONFIRMED, A569-A570; synthesis check as summarized in the accompanying artifacts) excludes the pure-swirl class by the sign of the canonical pressure on the axis, Pcan = -(1/(4 pi)) int abs(V)^2 abs(X - y)^(-3) dy < 0, against S -> 0 at the poles; with A561 this gives V = 0 and then U = 0 for the whole conditional class (2/5 < c < 1/2, every omega, global zero helicity, natural bounds, axisymmetric actual tail; Theorem AX, item 1d). The pressure tail has a multipole expansion: the moments of U x U - V x V of order k < 3p - 2 converge and S_t - S is a finite sum of rotating harmonic multipoles with rates r_k = (k+5)c - 2 plus O(e^{-gamma t}) for every gamma < 1 (A550, CONFIRMED; spectral analysis C38; no helicity). On an escaping regular zero-U.B patch, mu lies in {1} union {1 + r_k : k < 3p - 2} union [2, infinity), so a vortical carrier equilibrium in the target class has rho in {-(1-2c), -2(1-c)} union {-(k+3)c : k < 3p - 2} union (-infinity, -(3-2c)] (A551, CONFIRMED as necessary conditions); for omega != 0 and 1 < mu < 2 the single surviving multipole is a nonzero multiple of r^{-(k+3)} P_{k+2}(x_3/r) and the sheet lies on one of its Legendre zero cones (A552, CONFIRMED; this is symmetry of a pressure multipole, not of V, and does not activate A556). Along the vortex line through a vortical carrier equilibrium p (dynamical analysis B31-B34; global zero
helicity, U = o(r), no decay): a bounded half-line has a compact invariant limit set K with Omega = 0, H = H(p),
U.B = 0, grad H = -(1-2c)U, grad(U.B) = rho U and U != 0 on K; every invariant probability on K lives on its
equilibrium set; K contains no nonconstant periodic orbit; at each equilibrium q of K the plane U(q)^perp has real
eigenvalues lambda_- <= 0 < lambda_+ with sum 3c - rho, and a hyperbolic q with D Omega(q) != 0 has spectrum
{rho, rho + 1 + c, -(1-2c) - 2rho} with rho < -(1+c) (A540-A542, CONFIRMED; the collapse of K to one equilibrium is
proved only under an extra finite-network hypothesis, A542). At such a q the level carries a C^2 stream function
psi with B psi = -(1-2c+rho) psi, and a vortical vortex line that is a B-orbit converging to q needs
-2(1+c) <= rho < -(1+c) (A543, CONFIRMED); the reduced surface equations allow this whole window (A544, reduced
equations only). Two printed source statements were REFUTED: the stated monotonicity of sigma = rho/(rho+1+c) (it
increases, A545) and the use of a cited degree-3 polynomial jet as a certificate of compatibility with the global
class (A546). Unaudited parts of the synthesis checks: along an escaping orbit on W^u(p), the
area Jacobian is O(e^{2ct}), compatible with the weighted area law and Kelvin's theorem; explicit second-order jets
at rho = -2(1-2c), every omega, satisfy every low-order condition. The range rho <= -2(1-c) is open. At a nonzero irrotational
carrier equilibrium p in closure{Omega != 0}, write lambda = grad(U.B).grad H/abs(grad H)^2. For every
omega, with U = o(r) uniformly and no decay or derivative bound, every vortical point with grad H != 0 and U.B = 0
has lambda >= 1 (zero-U.B obstruction; A521, CONFIRMED; synthesis, the second-model review, check
as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; A413, A478 and A496 are used; the vortex saturation may be unbounded). Hence, when
D Omega(p) != 0, the second spectral family of A469 with rho > 0, which contains its whole bad range
rho >= 3(1-2c), is excluded for every omega, and in the first family with rho > 0 a small regular box around p has
{Omega = 0} = {U.B = 0} = {H = H(p)} (A522, CONFIRMED). The first positive family itself is not excluded, and the
first and second families with rho <= -2(1-2c), the first family with rho >= (1-2c)/2, and D Omega(p) = 0 remain
open. For a flat periodic witness with rho > 3c (this contains its upper bad range rho >= 2 - c), Omega vanishes on
both small local cylinders (A523, CONFIRMED); this gives no irrotational neighbourhood, and vortical points off the
two cylinders are not controlled. A further second-model review (single model; comparison summarized in the accompanying artifacts) adds: near a flat periodic orbit with rho > -(1-2c) and U != 0 no vortical point has
U.B = 0 (now A537, CONFIRMED); for rho < 0 (unaudited) no single regular vortical component of the level of the orbit has the orbit in its closure,
although infinitely many such components may accumulate on it; and on a compact H-level every regular vortical
point with U.B = 0 has lambda = 1 (now A536, CONFIRMED). It does not exclude a flat periodic witness. Synthesis claim CO27
(as summarized in the accompanying artifacts section 26; A536, CONFIRMED) carries A517-A518 from vortical equilibria to every connected
regular vortical level component Sigma on which U.B vanishes somewhere: lambda is constant on Sigma, at least 1, and
in the target scope (U -> 0, DU = O(r^(1/2)), 2/5 < c < 1/2) either equal to 1 or at least 2(1-c)/(1-2c), the second
case only on the level H_inf and with a regular arc of Z_E. At an irrotational carrier equilibrium with
D Omega(p) != 0 this gives: either Omega = 0 on the level piece of p (algebraically unexcluded only if
D Omega(p) = w u^T/abs(u)^2 with F w = (rho + 1 + c) w, so in the first family, or in the second family at rho = -1
or rho = -(1-2c)/3; no such local germ is constructed), or rho = -(1-2c) or rho <= -2(1-c). For a flat periodic
carrier orbit with U != 0 there is no nearby vortical point with U.B = 0 if rho > -(1-2c), nor, in the target scope,
if -2(1-c) < rho < -(1-2c) (A537, CONFIRMED as necessary conditions only). Left open by A537: separating levels,
D Omega(p) = 0, the strict lower range rho < -2(1-c), and nearby vortical points with U.B != 0. Two synthesis checks of the second-model review narrow these cases; both are CONFIRMED at their stated scopes (A559-A560 and A563-A566). At an irrotational carrier equilibrium with D Omega(p) != 0 (CO30, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; A563-A566): the separating case is not excluded at C^2 (explicit quadratic jets at omega = 0 satisfy divergence, curl, quadratic Cauchy transport and quadratic helicity; rechecked symbolically; higher-order obstructions only at isolated rho: no C^3 extension at rho = (c-2)/3 or -3/4 and no C^4 extension at c = 9/20, rho = -1, all at omega = 0 with local rank, A566; cubic compatibility jets and an analytic realization of the zero geometry at rho = -1, A565); if the level of p meets {Omega != 0} in the first family with rho <= -2(1-c), then rho <= -1 - c/4 when U is C^3 (the excluded interval is nonempty only for c > 4/9), and rho = -1 - (m-1)c/(m+2) for an integer m >= 2 or rho <= -(1+c) when U is C-infinity; the first family is not hyperbolic at rho = -(1+c); the second family, rho <= -(1+c) and D Omega(p) = 0 stay open. For a flat periodic orbit with rho >= 2 - c or rho <= -2(1-2c) (CO29, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A559, A560], with the lower-range stable-cylinder step repaired): no nonzero-pitch helically symmetric germ exists, and no axisymmetric one under the no-closed-vortex condition (A014 for global profiles), for every omega; if U is C^(n+2) and Omega has a nonzero transverse Taylor term of degree n along the orbit, a closed vortex orbit lies nearby, contradicting A014, so no real-analytic witness exists; for C-infinity U, Omega vanishes to infinite order along the orbit and on both local cylinders. General C^2 germs and infinitely flat nonsymmetric germs remain OPEN (A560); none is constructed.
Without helicity or decay assumptions, a carrier equilibrium in the
closure of {Omega != 0} has min Re spec DB <= 0, because Omega vanishes near any equilibrium whose spectrum has all
real parts in (0, 1+c), and the trace 3c is below 1+c (A473). For a flat periodic orbit with rho < 0 or rho > 3c,
Omega vanishes on the local unstable cylinder; if rho <= -2(1-2c), every nearby stable Bernoulli loop carries a zero
of Omega; if rho <= -(1+c), Omega vanishes on the local stable cylinder too (A474). Vortical approach from outside the
two cylinders is not excluded. On a box where grad H != 0, U.B != 0 and dH wedge d(U.B) = 0, the profile has the
exact local normal form U = f(H) grad psi - grad H/(1-2c) with B psi = 0, BH = -(1-2c)G(H), f'/f = 1/G and
Laplacian H = (1-2c) div(f grad psi), and conversely (A482, the accompanying artifacts; local and conditional; one G
around a whole orbit is not inferred). Two exact countermodels show that flatness with transport alone, or curl
geometry without Euler transport, does not exclude a flat periodic witness (A483). In prescribed product,
angular-periodic and warped ansatz forms of the vorticity near a central annulus, nodal barriers exclude every
reconstructing velocity (A486-A488, the auditor proofs extending the literature audit LIT111-LIT114, with a synthesis review; prescribed-ansatz
scope only). For the exact mixed flat-circle germ the second jet fails the necessary global rank test, but a harmonic
correction passes it on the circle and is removable at higher order (A491, the literature audit LIT107, with a synthesis review;
local jet scope only). No reduction of a general flat periodic orbit to these forms is known. Neither witness type is excluded, and none of this applies when the helicity changes
sign.
Part (ii) holds in the same C^r class under either form of the condition (CONDITIONAL on it; A422 for the global form
and A432 for the componentwise form, both confirmed as conditional theorems; the auditor, with synthesis reviews): for an
integer r >= 2, U in C^r and P in C^1, decaying, 2/5 <= c < 1/2, every omega and Gamma_E < r(1-2c) for every
component E of {Omega != 0}, one sign of U.Omega on each D_nu forces U = 0. After coverage the argument uses only U in
C^2 and P in C^1, and it assumes no density of {Omega != 0}, mixing, finite energy or derivative decay. In particular
a C^2 decaying profile with Gamma_E < 2(1-2c) for every E and U.Omega >= 0 everywhere (or <= 0 everywhere) vanishes.
Neither part is asserted from C^2 regularity and decay alone: at the C^2 baseline of section 0 (H0, H1), which the
prompt asks us to start from, both the coverage step and the unrestricted nonexistence problem remain open (A318).
The given-basin theorem A278 and the recurrence argument A283 do hold at C^2. A complete proof of (ii) and (iii)
from the coverage theorems is written out in 2D.
(iii) Levelwise refinement (the auditor; A326-A328). Write H = P + abs(U)^2/2 + (Ay).U, so that
Omega.grad H = -(1-2c) U.Omega. If U.Omega is nonzero somewhere on an invariant open set D of the recurrent vortex
flow, there is an open interval I of real numbers such that every b in I is attained by H at two points of one
recurrent vortex orbit in D, with U.Omega > 0 at one point and U.Omega < 0 at the other (A326, an abstract C^1
statement). Hence the hypothesis of (ii) can be weakened to: on each D_nu and each level {H = b}, U.Omega has at most
one sign, the sign allowed to depend on nu and b (A327; same class and range of c as (ii), and at finite r under
A312 or A373). For C^2 uniformly sublinear profiles, 0 < c < 1/2 and every omega, the integrals of (U.Omega)_+ and
(U.Omega)_- over E intersect {H in I} are equal, as numbers in [0, infinity], for every vortex-invariant measurable
set E and every Borel set I of reals (A328). This is a balance of pushforwards, not pointwise vanishing, and it does
not imply finite helicity.

1d. Conditional nonexistence for helicity-free profiles: (i) with an axisymmetric leading velocity tail (Theorem AX);
(ii) without symmetry, when the tail scalar S is 0 or abs(S)^(-beta) is locally integrable (Theorem DA in its
strengthened form, A705-A708; the original A598 form also assumed exterior-dense vorticity and an A2 weight
abs(S)^beta). Both are CONDITIONAL; both
implications are PROVED. Theorem AX: the auditor A570 CONFIRMED, with A561 and A569; the literature audit LIT147 and LIT150; the audit summary in
the accompanying artifacts; synthesis check as summarized in the accompanying artifacts. Theorem DA: the auditor A598
CONFIRMED, with A593-A597; the literature audit LIT151-LIT154; synthesis reading as summarized in the accompanying artifacts.

Theorem AX. Let 2/5 < c < 1/2, omega real, p = (1-c)/c, A = cI - omega J, L = (1-c)I + omega J. Let U in C^2(R^3),
P in C^1(R^3) solve div U = 0 and (1-c)U + DU(Ay + U) + omega JU + grad P = 0, with U.curl U = 0 everywhere,
U(y) -> 0 uniformly and DU(y) = O(abs(y)^(1/2)) (equivalently the natural bounds abs(U) <= C(1+r)^(-p),
abs(DU) <= C(1+r)^(-p-1), by A498, A476, A492). Let V(x) = lim_{t -> infinity} e^(tL) U(e^(tA) x) be the actual leading
velocity tail (A516, A530-A531). If V is axisymmetric about the rotation axis, then U = 0.

Proof outline. (1) The natural-tail package (A516, A530-A531, A533, A538-A539) gives V in C^(1,alpha) off 0 for every
alpha < 1, twisted homogeneous of degree -p, with div V = 0, V.curl V = 0, the canonical pressure
P2 = d_i d_j Gamma * (V_i V_j), curl V.grad S = 0 for S = P2 - abs(V)^2/2, and the rank condition
grad k x grad S = 0 on {curl V != 0}, k = (Ax).V (the limit of A413, as in A534 and A556). For axisymmetric V the
twisted homogeneity is ordinary homogeneity, and P2 is axisymmetric. (2) A561: such a tail is 0 or pure swirl,
V = r^(-p) F(z) e_phi / sqrt(1 - z^2) with F of one strict sign and S = C r^(-2p) abs(F)^(2p/(p-1)), C < 0. (3) A569: at
every nonzero point X of the axis, P2(X) = -(1/(4 pi)) int abs(V(y))^2 abs(X - y)^(-3) dy, finite and negative if
V != 0, and no other homogeneous pressure of degree -2p solves the Poisson equation (1 < p < 3/2). A continuous
azimuthal field vanishes on the axis, so F -> 0 at the poles, S -> 0 and P2 -> 0 there: V = 0. (4) A570: with V = 0
and abs(DU U + grad P) <= C r^(-2p-1) (A516), integrating d/dt[e^(tL) U(e^(tA) x)] = -e^(tL) (DU U + grad P)(e^(tA) x)
gives abs(U) <= C r^(-2p-1), since (1-c) - c(2p+1) = -1; so U is in L^2, and the energy identity
(1 - 5c/2) abs(U)^2 + div[(Ay + U) abs(U)^2/2 + (P - Pinf) U] = 0 with vanishing cutoff fluxes gives U = 0.

Hypotheses beyond the problem: global zero helicity U.curl U = 0 (H9), the derivative bound DU = O(r^(1/2)) (H3;
whether U -> 0 implies it is item 6, OPEN) and axisymmetry of the actual tail V (H7; required of V only, not of U or
of a pressure multipole; not implied by anything known). The witness classification of item 1c is not used, and
the result holds for every omega. Nonsymmetric tails: if every zero of S has a C^1 surface or curve chart with
abs(S) comparable to a power of the distance below the thresholds of A567, the lower escaping rates are excluded
(A567-A568, CONDITIONAL), but V = 0 does not follow. Whether every twisted homogeneous tail with the five
properties in (1) vanishes, without symmetry, is OPEN; by (4) a positive answer would give U = 0 for every
helicity-free profile with DU = O(r^(1/2)) in 2/5 < c < 1/2 and every omega. Local analysis cannot settle this: for every omega there are
real-analytic nonaxisymmetric fields on an equatorial band with all five properties and a regular zero of S where curl V != 0
(synthesis CO33, the second-model review, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; A590 CONFIRMED as local existence only; with a zero of S of any even order, the literature audit LIT155, A599). The global constraints available are
pole regularity, uniqueness of the twisted pressure for 1 < p < 3/2, and the mean identity: the spherical mean of S is
negative for every nonzero tail (A591, CONFIRMED). Global hypotheses that close the tail problem are confirmed: Theorem DA below.

Theorem DA. Let 2/5 < c < 1/2, omega real, and let U, P be as in Theorem AX: U in C^2, P in C^1, div U = 0, the
profile equation, U.curl U = 0 everywhere, U(y) -> 0 uniformly and DU(y) = O(abs(y)^(1/2)) (or DU bounded, or the natural bounds, or the one-sided strain
Dini bound of A601).
Let V be the actual leading velocity tail, P2 the canonical tail pressure and S = P2 - abs(V)^2/2. Assume
(a) {curl U != 0} is dense in some exterior region {abs(y) > R0} (equivalently, by A603, {curl V != 0} is dense in
    R^3 minus 0), or U is real-analytic on some exterior region; and
(b) S is identically 0, or b = abs(S)^beta, beta = (p-1)/(2p), is a local A2 weight on R^3 minus 0 (b > 0 almost
    everywhere, b and 1/b locally integrable, products of their ball averages bounded on each compact subset).
Then U = 0. No symmetry of U or of V is assumed.
Strengthened form (the literature audit LIT175, CONFIRMED [A705-A708]). Hypothesis (a) is unnecessary, and (b) can be replaced by:
S is identically 0, or abs(S)^(-beta) is locally integrable on R^3 minus 0 (value +infinity on {S = 0}); still weaker,
G = 0 almost everywhere on {h = 0} and int_{h != 0} abs(G) abs(h)^(-beta) dA < infinity, with G = curl V and h = S on
S^2. The rest of the hypotheses (zero helicity, decay, derivative or natural bounds) are unchanged. Proof (A705-A707):
A360 gives a positive-volume set B of points whose tail-vortex arcs reach 0 within a time T; the partial W flow
F_t = Xi o Gamma_t o Xi^(-1) is a C^1 volume-preserving map (W(Xi y) = D Xi(y) Omega(y), A209-A210); S is constant
on every arc (A531), so abs(S) < M along them; a radial cutoff chi_eps, Tonelli and the change of variables give
0 < abs(B) <= C T eps^(-(p-1)) int_{abs(h) < M (2 eps)^(2p)} abs(G) dA, the critical exponent cancels exactly, and
dominated convergence makes the right side tend to 0. Necessary form (A708): a nonzero profile in this class has
int_{abs(h) < s} abs(G) dA >= C_* s^beta for all small s. LIT176 (CONFIRMED [A709-A711] at its scope): the exponent is
attained by a singular kinematic swirl with exact finite-time core return (it fails the canonical Poisson equation;
not an Euler profile). LIT177 (CONFIRMED [A721-A722] at its scope): the weighted condition holds at scalar nodes where
G vanishes and abs(S) is comparable to dist^m on a smooth curve (m beta < 2), at a point (m beta < 3) or at a transverse
two-curve crossing (sum of max(m_j beta - 1, 0) < 1); flat nodes, cusps and tangent crossings are not covered.
Synthesis CO43 (CONFIRMED [A730-A735] with scope; as summarized in the accompanying artifacts) runs the same stopped-flow bound with any continuous first integral f of W of twisted degree -1, in particular abs(k)^(1/(p-1)) with k = (Ax).V (k is C^1 with grad k = Ax x curl V - (1-2c)V and constant on every W curve, A702): a nonzero profile in this class has int_{abs(K) < tau} abs(G) dA >= C_* tau for small tau (K = k on S^2), the concentration localizes (almost every tail-vortex arc accumulates angularly at the set where it fails to be o(tau)), and under the nodal premise {k = 0} in {curl V = 0} that set lies in the zero set of V on S^2, so such a profile has a tail stagnation ray and is 0 if V has no zero; isolated nondegenerate critical points of K are also excluded.
The literature audit LIT178 (CONFIRMED [A736-A740]): global zero helicity makes Q = P - Pinf - abs(U)^2/2 constant on complete
original vortex lines, and the commutation Phi_t Gamma_s = Gamma_(exp((1+c)t)s) Phi_t with the actual limit
exp(2(1-c)t) Q(Phi_t y) -> S(Xi y) gives equal S values on all escaping pieces of one original vortex line, also when
the line crosses the scattering core. Hence F = S o Xi extends C^1 off the compact null set K_Omega of points whose
whole vortex lines stay in the core (A737), with volume{abs(F) > s} = (s^(-q)/3) int abs(h)^q, q = 3/(2p) (A738), weak
transport div(F Omega) = 0 and div(F B) = (5c-2)F on all of R^3 (A739), original vortex recurrence on its superlevel
sets, and: a nonzero value of F forces backward B approach to K_Omega, so K_Omega empty, or F locally bounded near every
point, gives U = 0 (A740). The literature audit LIT179 (CONFIRMED [A786-A789] at the stated hypotheses): on each component of {Omega != 0, F != 0} off K_Omega the
levels are connected, H = h(s), Q = q(s) with s = abs(F), and ell = eta int q(s) s^(-eta-1) ds; so a tail point with
W != 0, k = 0 and S != 0 (a failure of the nodal premise) forces Q to take both signs along every B trajectory of
that original component. This is a compatibility condition, not an exclusion. Confirmed are the C^1 rank lemma (A786), the extension L of k o Xi through original vortex excursions (A787), the connected-level normal form with the exact moment (A788; its discounted identity is A426) and the sign change (A789); common k = S = 0 nodes and a pressure-sign theorem remain open. The sign change also holds trajectory by trajectory from A426: k(xi) = a int e^(at) Q(Y(t)) dt along an escaping B trajectory Y with asymptotic amplitude xi.
The literature audit LIT181 (CONFIRMED [A810-A814]; global zero helicity and the natural velocity and gradient bounds): the extension L of k o Xi is C^1 off the joint core, vortex invariant and satisfies L o Phi_t = exp(-at) L (A810). On a connected component M of {L = 0} on which dL and Omega do not vanish, H - P_inf = Q = g = 0, dH = dL and dQ = 0 (A811; gauge A1278), and U = b grad H, B x Omega = (1 + ab) grad H with one constant b != 0 on all of M (A812). Hence every regular vortical tail node (k = 0, W != 0, grad k != 0) has S = 0 and V = b grad k != 0 (A814; this is the actual-profile form of CO45(c)). If 1 + ab = 0, then B = tau Omega on M with Omega.tau = 1 + c, and every vortex line in M crosses exactly one carrier equilibrium (A813). If 1 + ab != 0 (the literature audit LIT182, CONFIRMED [A815-A818]), the closure of M stays regular (A815), M is closed and properly embedded in R^3 (A816), M is an annulus carrying exactly one periodic carrier orbit, which is the intersection of M with the core, and every other carrier orbit in M escapes forward (A817); each tail vortex arc over M has one end at the origin, reached in finite vortex time, and one end at infinity (A818). So in the nonparallel branch no tail vortex arc over M returns to the origin at both ends (A818 is stated for that branch; the same endpoint pattern in the parallel branch is part of the literature audit LIT183, SUBMITTED); this is compatible with the almost-everywhere core return of A360, which concerns almost every point of R^3 and not a prescribed null surface. Neither branch was excluded by these facts (A819 OPEN); both are excluded by LIT187-LIT188 below (A885, A896-A897). The literature audit LIT183 (CONFIRMED [A862-A864]): in the nonparallel branch the annulus gives exactly two distinct closed regular vortical angular nodal curves with the same b and least carrier period T (A863), so nonparallel regular arcs cannot end at critical or irrotational angular points, and both angular vortex fluxes and both collar periods of V/k have magnitude abs(1 + ab) T (A864); in the parallel branch the tail vortex orbit is exp(A log(1 + (1+c)s/tau0)/(1+c)) z0, with one end at the origin in finite vortex time and one at infinity in infinite time (A862), so every regular vortical tail node has this endpoint pattern. The literature audit LIT184 (CONFIRMED [A865-A868]): in the parallel branch M = P0 x R with Omega = d/dzeta and B = (1+c) zeta d/dzeta, where P0 is a bounded connected embedded curve of carrier equilibria (a circle or a line), closed relative to O, whose missing ambient boundary points lie in K_Omega with grad H and U nonzero there (A865; boundedness does not give compactness); the two open sets of points of P0 whose vortex half-line of a given sign escapes cover P0, and their components correspond exactly to the regular vortical angular nodal components of that sign (A866-A867); a compact angular component forces P0 to be a circle and every half-line of that sign to escape, with no conclusion for the other sign (A867); a nonescaping half-line converges to one irrotational carrier equilibrium with U != 0, rate -a and D Omega = 0 (A868, from A658-A659). Neither branch is excluded by these facts alone (A869 OPEN); see LIT187-LIT188 and A897 below. The literature audit LIT185 (CONFIRMED [A875-A876]): for every finite omega an explicit axisymmetric ansatz with swirl gives an analytic cone over a full azimuthal band satisfying all local necessary tail equations with k = 0, S > 0, V != 0, W != 0 (type (h1)); its full radial momentum residual is -(3p+1) - 2p(omega/c)^2 < 0, so it is not a local profile, and no global realization is known (A877 OPEN). The literature audit LIT186 (CONFIRMED [A878-A881]; A882 OPEN): near a regular vortical nodal sheet M, Q = O(abs(H - P_inf)^q), so D^2 Q = 0 on the closure of M (A879; the finite-level comparison of scalar germs holds for all finite carrier times, A878); through the Poisson equation this gives 2 abs(sym DU)^2 = U.curl Omega on M, which excludes first-order-flat vorticity points of the closure of M (A880), and in the parallel branch both signs of every vortex line in M escape (A881). The literature audit LIT187 (CONFIRMED [A883-A886]; A887 OPEN): on a regular vortical nodal sheet the surface vorticity U.curl Omega = 2 abs(sym DU)^2 (A1282) is one-signed, and with vanishing boundary circulations Stokes' theorem on an exhaustion then forces sym DU = 0 on the sheet; then abs(Omega(Phi_t y)) = exp(-t) abs(Omega(y)) there, which contradicts compact backward trapping (A883; no finite-area premise); actual scattering gives the O(R) nodal boundary length the exhaustion needs (A884). Hence the nonparallel branch (A) is impossible (A885: a compact annular exhaustion exists and both boundary circulations vanish), and in the parallel branch a compact P0 would give the same exhaustion, so P0 cannot be compact (A886). The literature audit LIT188 (CONFIRMED [A894-A896]): the missing ambient boundary points of P0 are irrotational but not first-order flat (A894), pressure flatness orients both sides of P0 away from such a point (A895), and so P0 is a compact embedded C^1 circle (A896), contradicting A886. Together (A897, CONFIRMED): for every real omega, in the class of Theorem DA (global zero helicity, U in C^2, P in C^1, U decaying, DU = O(abs(y)^(1/2)) or the natural bounds), the actual tail has no regular vortical node, that is, no point with k = 0, grad k != 0 and W != 0. Critical vortical nodes, the global helicity premise, the derivative premise and the decay-only conjecture remain open (A898 OPEN). The literature audit LIT189 (CONFIRMED [A899-A900]; A901 OPEN): nonzero analytic local tails exist on an open common zero set of k and grad k with W != 0 (critical vortical nodes of type (h3)); their full momentum residual is -(p+1) - 2p sigma^2 < 0, so they are local countertests only, and they decide nothing about actual critical nodes (A901 OPEN). Synthesis CO46 (CONFIRMED [A913-A915]; A916 OPEN; as summarized in the accompanying artifacts): call x a critical vortical node if grad k(x) = 0 and W(x) != 0; then k(x) = 0 and Ax x W(x) = aV(x). In the class of Theorem DA: (N) holds on an open twisted cone if and only if the cone contains no critical vortical node (A913); the concentration set Sigma lies in the closure of the critical vortical nodes union the flat zeros of V in supp G, so U = 0 if the tail has neither (A914; the closure is essential); and U = 0 if V has no zero on S^2 and W is parallel to Ax at every critical vortical node with S = 0 (A915). Whether critical vortical nodes or flat zeros of V in supp G occur for actual profiles is OPEN (A916). An independent proof of the regular-node exclusion (the auditor referee, the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A917-A920]; A921 OPEN): a C^2 scalar has finite integral of abs(grad F) over its regular zero set in a compact ball, and a parallel nodal sheet cannot be entirely forward trapped (A917); on P0 the tangent field T = Omega x U + (2 omega/(1+c)) U_3 Omega satisfies T log abs(Omega)^2 >= 4[1 + c^2 + (1-c)^2] for every omega (A918), so a positive maximum of abs(Omega) on P0, which lies in P0 by relative closure, gives a contradiction without compactness of P0 (A919); a cut at fixed vortex time gives vanishing circulation for the annular Stokes argument, the cycle strain bound int_cycle abs(E)^2 >= 3T/2 holds, and Delta Q >= 0 on M suffices for the annular exclusion (A920); the weaker criterion Delta Q >= 0 on P0 alone needs a closure premise (A921 OPEN). The literature audit LIT190 (CONFIRMED [A922-A924]; A925 OPEN): let z be a vortical tail node (k(z) = 0, W(z) != 0) that is not an interior point of {k = 0}. Then z lifts to a whole joint leaf N of the original profile (generated by the carrier and vortex flows) on which H - P_inf = Q = g = 0 and dH = dQ = 0 as ambient differentials (A922-A923; finite affine flow commutation reaches the whole leaf, including core segments); if moreover V(z) != 0, then U is nowhere zero on N, B and Omega are independent there, and N is an immersed two-dimensional leaf (A924; properness and embeddedness not claimed). So every critical vortical node of type (h3) with V != 0 has a critical original leaf with vanishing first jets of H - P_inf and Q. Whether these leaves are excluded, or have D^2 H = D^2 Q = 0, is OPEN (A925). The literature audit LIT191 (CONFIRMED [A933-A934]; A935 OPEN): if dL = 0 on a vortical periodic carrier orbit in O, then L = 0 on an open neighbourhood of that orbit (A933); so in the actual class every vortical periodic carrier orbit in O lies in the interior of {L = 0} (A934, with A897); cycles inside open zero regions and cycles in the joint core are not excluded (A935). spectral analysis C44 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A936-A941]; A942 OPEN; historical, the configuration is empty by LIT195 below, A960-A964, A1864), same class: a vortical zero of L with dH != 0 is either interior to {L = 0} or a regular node with dL = dH and H - P_inf = Q = dQ = 0 (A936, agreeing with A922). Let y0 in O be a vortical zero of L with dL(y0) = 0 that is not interior to {L = 0}, and let Cbar be the closure of its joint leaf. Then on Cbar H - P_inf = Q = g = 0, dH = dQ = dg = 0, the Hessians of H and Q are multiples of U U^T, and the Kelvin covector transport D Phi_t(y)^T U(Phi_t y) = exp(-at) U(y) is exact (A937); U is nowhere zero on Cbar, so aU = B x Omega != 0, and Cbar lies in O, is closed with empty interior and consists of joint leaves of the same type (A938, using A478 and A118); at every noninterior critical vortical tail node S = dS = 0 and V = D Xi^(-T) U != 0, so aV = Ax x W != 0 (A939; this removes the premise V != 0 of A924, so a noninterior critical node with V = 0 does not occur); for omega = 0 no such node exists (A940, from B(abs(y)^2) = 2 abs(B)^2/c on a compact backward limit set); for every omega every leaf of Cbar is intrinsically a plane and Cbar contains no carrier cycle (A941, from A934 and A143). The exclusion of these plane leaves for omega != 0, their properness and their second-order flatness were left OPEN (A942); LIT195 below shows that the whole configuration is empty for every omega (A960-A964). The literature audit LIT192 and LIT193 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts and as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A953-A958]; A959 OPEN; historical, the configuration is empty by LIT195, A960-A964, A1864), same class and configuration: at a point of Cbar with D^2 H != 0 the critical set of H is locally one plaque of the joint leaf of y0 (A953), so the compact backward limit set of y0 contains a point with D^2 H = 0 (A954); abs(L(y + v)) <= C_alpha abs(v)^(1+alpha) at every point y of Cbar for every alpha < 1 (A955); D^2 Q = mu D^2 H with 0 <= mu <= 1 wherever D^2 H != 0 (A956); D^2 H = 0 forces D^2 Q = 0, and simultaneous vanishing is invariant under both flows (A957). Stronger form (auditor, A958): writing D^2 H = h U U^T and D^2 Q = q U U^T on Cbar, the Kelvin law gives d/dt h(Phi_t y) = a(h + q)(Phi_t y), so exp(2at) abs(h(y)) <= abs(h(Phi_t y)) <= exp(at) abs(h(y)) for t <= 0, and every backward carrier limit point of every point of Cbar has D^2 H = D^2 Q = 0. Hence Cbar contains complete plane leaves on which H - P_inf and Q vanish to second order, and on them the pressure Poisson equation gives U.curl Omega = 2 abs(sym DU)^2. A Stokes argument on such a leaf, as in the regular case (A883-A886), needs an exhaustion with controlled boundary circulation, properness or recurrence; none is established, and critical nodes, open zero regions and the conjecture remain unresolved (A959).

Synthesis the second-model review (check as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; audited directly in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A947-A951]; A952 OPEN), local tails: near a point with V != 0 the plane field orthogonal to V is integrable and k = A0 K(f) with A0 > 0 and f a transverse coordinate, so critical nodes are multiple roots of the one-variable function K (A947); for every c, omega and every integer m >= 2 there are analytic vortical local tail germs with k = exp(l) f^m, S = 0 and P2 = abs(V)^2/2, and at c = 3/7 a germ with m = 2 and S = k^8 (A948); the second-order scalar equation for k has principal matrix (abs(V)^2 + qS)I - V V^T, degenerate in the direction of V where S = 0, so no uniformly elliptic minimum principle is available at a critical node (A949); a conditional accumulation argument (A950) has an antecedent already excluded by A897; the normalized scalar system H = h(s), Q = q_C(s) of an open zero region of L is consistent (explicit pair, A951). None of these local results excludes actual critical nodes or open zero regions (A952 OPEN).

The literature audit LIT194 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A966-A969]), same configuration: on the invariant stratum of Cbar where the jets of H - P_inf and Q vanish through order m-1, both m-jets are pure normal tensors with D^m Q = mu D^m H and 1 - m/2 <= mu <= 1, zero m-jets are invariant under both flows, and every compact invariant subset of Cbar is flat through every order the regularity allows; its analytic corollary is superseded by LIT195. The literature audit LIT195 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A960-A964, A970]; A965 OPEN), class HF with the natural bounds, every omega: a vortical zero of L in O that is not an interior point of {L = 0} does not exist. Proof: on the compact backward limit set of such a point (inside Cbar by C44) the Kelvin law gives the bracket DB N - DN B = -aN + beta B + delta Omega for N = U/abs(U)^2, hence a bounded moving frame Z = N + bB + d Omega with D Phi_t Z = exp(-at) Z o Phi_t and det(Z, B, Omega) = a; a contraction in an exp(at)-weighted space gives a C^1 stable curve through each point with exact rate exp(-at); the uniform C^1 vanishing modulus of L there and L o Phi_t = exp(-at) L force L = 0 on the stable curve, and saturating the curve by the two flows (a map of Jacobian a) makes the base point interior to {L = 0}, a contradiction (A960-A962; A970 is the auditor's independent stable-curve proof). Consequences (A963-A964): every vortical zero of L in O, and every vortical zero of k on R^3 minus 0, is an interior point of its zero set; on each connected component of {Omega != 0} in O, L vanishes identically or has one strict sign, and the same holds for k on the components of {W != 0}. The full conjecture is not claimed (A965). The synthesis the second-model review (single model, not submitted) gives a second proof of the same exclusion by hyperbolic closing and agrees with LIT192-LIT193. The literature audit LIT196 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A973-A974]; A975 OPEN), same class: every boundary point of the interior of {k = 0} is a flat zero of V (V = DV = 0) in supp W (A973: W = V = grad k = 0 there by A963 and continuity; a nonzero symmetric trace-free DV with DV(Ax) = 0 would make the angular zero isolated, which the boundary topology excludes; an irrotational neighbourhood is excluded by harmonicity). Hence, with T-flat = {V = DV = 0} intersected with supp W on S^2: if U != 0 and T-flat is empty, then k = 0 on all of R^3 minus 0 (A974). The branch k = 0 everywhere, T-flat and the premises remain (A975). spectral analysis C45 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A976-A979]; A980 OPEN as a stronger uniform reading), same configuration and proved without LIT195: D^2 Q = 0 on the whole critical closure, with one-sided germs H - P_inf ~ L, Q = O(abs(L)^q) (A976); D^2 H = h U U^T with h(Gamma_s Phi_t y) = exp(at) h(y), every compact invariant subset Hessian-flat, and one common alpha-limit set for all backward orbits of a joint leaf (A977); U.curl Omega = 2 abs(sym DU)^2 on the closure, with invariant strain averages (A978); the leaf Stokes formula d(Omega.dx) = 2a abs(sym DU)^2 dtheta dzeta and no annular leaf with both halves escaping (A979). As exclusions these are superseded by A963: the configuration is empty for every omega (LIT195, A960-A964), and these statements are recorded as mechanisms (A1864). Synthesis CO47 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A999-A1002]; A1003 OPEN; A1004 CONFIRMED at its stated kinematic scope), same class: if U != 0 and T-flat is empty, so that k = 0 everywhere, then V = a^(-1) Ax x W, the interior of {W = 0} is empty, and the Poincare-Hopf theorem for the projection of V to S^2 (V is orthogonal to Aw, and w.Aw = c > 0) gives a zero w0 of V with W(w0) = lambda Aw0, lambda != 0, and abs(W(w0))^2 >= 2 abs(sym DV(w0))^2; there S = P2 = 0, and the twisted ray through w0 is a vortex line of W on which V = 0. These are the tail data of an escaping (W1v) vortex half-line (item 1e, A602, A972).

The literature audit LIT197 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A1005-A1008]; A1009 OPEN), same class: W is differentiable at each zero of W with DW = DXi DOmega DXi^(-1) (A1005); local pressure rigidity: if v(0) = curl v(0) = 0 for a local solution (v, pi) of the stationary Euler system and s - s(0) >= -eps abs(v)^2 on a ball, s = pi - abs(v)^2/2, with eps < alpha/(2(1+alpha)) and v in C^(1,alpha), then v = 0 near 0 (A1006); at every zero of V outside the closure of int{k = 0}, W = DW = 0 and the original Omega and D Omega vanish at its preimage (A1007), and every neighbourhood contains an open irrotational patch or infinitely many vortical components (A1008). The literature audit LIT198 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A1012-A1015]; A1016 OPEN), local tails on a twisted cone with k = 0 (div V = 0, the Poisson equation for P2, W.grad S = 0): a zero w0 of V with W(w0) != 0 and abs(W(w0))^2 >= 2 abs(sym DV(w0))^2 (nonnegative index of the projected field) has sym DV(w0) = 0, S = dS = D^2 S = 0, index +1 and abs(S) <= C d(w, w0)^(2q) (a pure rotation zero; A1012-A1014); in the global alternative k = 0 everywhere without T-flat there are at least two such zeros (A1015). The auditor adds that at every local vortical zero of V the strain ratio lies in {0, q-1, 2q-1} (A1017). The literature audit LIT199 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A1018-A1022]; A1023 OPEN), same class as CO47: an actual vortical zero w0 of V (then W(w0) = lambda Aw0 with lambda != 0, by A963) lifts to a vortex half-line of the original profile that leaves a vortical carrier equilibrium p0, reached in finite vortex time (A1018); the angular derivative at w0 of the projected tail vorticity is similar to -lambda DB(p0) on the quotient by Omega(p0), with spectrum {-lambda rho, lambda(a + rho)} (A1019); since rho < -a (A496, A602), every actual vortical zero of V is a nondegenerate saddle of the projected field (A1020); hence, with LIT196 and CO47, U = 0 if V has no flat zero (V = DV = 0) in supp W on S^2 (A1021, which supersedes the alternative "k = 0 everywhere" of A974; A1049). Synthesis CO48 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts section 4; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A1024-A1026]): the trace identity tr D_S Z(w0) = a lambda at such a zero (A1024), and a local omega = 0 tail on a narrow cone with a pure rotation zero of index +1 (A1025), so the original equilibrium in LIT199 cannot be replaced by local tail equations. The literature audit LIT200 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A1041-A1045], with A1022; A1046 OPEN), same class: at the equilibrium p0 of an actual vortical zero w0 of V, rho = -b = -2(1-c) exactly, spec DB(p0) = {kappa, -b, 1}, the strain ratio at w0 is 2q - 1, and S = P2 = 0 at w0 with grad S != 0; along the escaping vortex line exp(-(2-c)t) abs(U) and exp(t) abs(Omega) have positive finite limits (A1044). The literature audit LIT201 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A1050-A1057]; A1058 OPEN), same class: with T0 = {V = DV = 0, S = 0} intersected with supp W on S^2, a nonzero profile has T0 nonempty (A1057). Proof outline: let Z = int{k = 0}, V0 = 1_Z V and E0 the angular support of V0; on {S != 0} the tangential part of V0 is abs(S)^eta grad f, where f solves a uniformly elliptic planar equation with Lipschitz principal part and bounded drift (A1051-A1052), so its zeros there are isolated with negative index (Alessandrini and Magnanini 1992, A1050); unique continuation puts the boundary of E0 in T0 (A1053); if E0 = S^2 and T0 is empty, every zero of the tangential field is isolated with negative index (A1020 at vortical zeros with S = 0), against Poincare-Hopf (A1054); if E0 is empty, the nodal premise holds and the joint stopped-flow bound int_{abs(K) < C1 tau, abs(S) < C2 tau^q} abs(G) dA >= C0 tau (A1055) localizes at T0 (A1056). Excluding T0, or showing S = 0 at every point of T-flat, is OPEN (A1058). The literature audit LIT202 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A1062-A1066]; A1067 OPEN), same class: the nodal premise (N) is equivalent to V0 = 0, that is E0 empty (A1062); at a point with V = DV = S = grad S = 0 the pressure Hessian exists, is trace free, annihilates Aw and, if nonzero, restricts to an angular saddle (A1063); a nonzero quadratic pressure jet has angular sublevel area O(eps(1 + abs(log eps))) (A1064); the joint mass is at least C tau and, under (N) with T2 empty, o(tau) (A1065); so under (N) a nonzero profile has a point of T2 = {V = DV = 0, P2 = grad P2 = D^2 P2 = 0} in supp W, and T2 is compact (A1066). Synthesis CO49 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts section 4; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts): a second proof of the index lemma of LIT201 by the Bers-Vekua similarity principle, with local index -n, n >= 1 (A1077, CONFIRMED); the normal form V = abs(S)^eta grad psi on {k = 0, S != 0} and the component constants (A1078, CONFIRMED); local analytic T-flat germs with k = 0 and S != 0 whose flat zero has index -m, for every c, omega and m >= 2 (A1079, CONFIRMED; not a global tail, a T0 example or a profile); every point of T0 is a limit of points with S < -eps abs(V)^2, for each eps < 1/4 (A1080, CONFIRMED); in the branch E0 = S^2 small neighbourhoods of T0 carry total index at least 2 (A1083, CONFIRMED). The further inference that P2 < 0 near every point of T0 was REFUTED (A1081, by the polynomial steady pair v = (x1^2 + x2^2)(-x2, x1, 0), pi = (x1^2 + x2^2)^3/6, which has the deficit with pi >= 0); the actual-tail sign is OPEN (A1082), and A1085 records that CO49 does not close T0. The literature audit LIT205 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; SUBMITTED; synthesis check as summarized in the accompanying artifacts section 3, no gap found, and the second-model review summarized in the accompanying artifacts is an independent derivation): if k = 0 near a point x0 of T0, V and P2 are smooth near x0, V vanishes to a finite order m >= 2 and its leading term is nonzero off the Ax0 direction, then the index of the angular field at x0 is at most 0 (the leading order of grad S x V = qSW at an angular minimum of the definite stream polynomial, then the leading Poisson equation at degree 2m); so in the branch k = 0 everywhere U = 0 if this holds at every point of T0. spectral analysis C46 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A1086-A1096]; A1099 OPEN), same class; call a point densely vortical if {W != 0} is dense near it: on an open set with dense vorticity S grad k = eta k grad S, the ratio S abs(k)^(-q) is constant on each local nonzero component of k, and S = 0 at zeros of k outside Z (A1086); at a densely vortical zero of V outside closure(Z), W = S = P2 = grad P2 = 0 and no neighbourhood satisfies S >= -C abs(k)^q (A1087), so infinitely many domains with negative constants unbounded below meet every neighbourhood (A1088); a pointwise Poisson expansion (A1089) and a count of finitely many connected sign sectors (A1090) give vanishing of P2 and S to every order below 4 at such a flat zero (A1091); every densely vortical point of the boundary of Z has grad P2 = D^2 P2 = 0 and P2, S = O(r^beta) for every beta < 4 (A1094); a densely vortical zero of V outside Z is flat (A1095). Together: every densely vortical zero of V outside Z has V = DV = W = P2 = grad P2 = D^2 P2 = 0, and P2 and S vanish there to every order below 4 (A1096). The conditional alternatives C46(e)-(f) are correct algebra but vacuous in this class (A1092-A1093). Zeros inside Z, accumulating irrotational patches and pressure of order 4 or higher are not covered (A1099 OPEN). The literature audit LIT206 (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; SUBMITTED) states the same conclusion by a different sector argument.
