Proof outline (the accompanying artifacts and the companion proofs of A593-A597).
(1) Rank transfer (A595; the literature audit LIT152). With H = P + abs(U)^2/2 + (Ay).U, g = U.(Ay + U) and R = H - g =
P - abs(U)^2/2, A413 gives grad H x grad R = 0 on {Omega != 0}, and density extends it by continuity to the exterior
region. Under the scaling of A516, e^(at)(H - Pinf) and e^(2(1-c)t)(R - Pinf), evaluated at e^(tA)x, converge in C^1
to k = (Ax).V and S (since a - 2(1-c) = -1), and both rescaled gradients are the original gradients multiplied by
the same matrix e^(tA^T) and by scalars. Hence grad k x grad S = 0 on all of R^3 minus 0, including any open
irrotational part of the tail. If U is real-analytic on the exterior and {Omega != 0} is not dense there, Omega = 0 on
the whole exterior; then {Omega != 0} is a bounded open set invariant under the carrier flow, whose Jacobian is
e^(3ct), so it is empty, and U is a decaying harmonic field, U = 0. (2) If S = 0 identically, the mean identity
int_{S^2} S = -[(3p-2) int abs(V.n)^2 + (p+1) int abs(V - (V.n)n)^2]/(2p) (A591) gives V = 0. (3) Otherwise A596
(LIT154; for 1/3 < c < 1/2): a C^1 divergence-free twisted homogeneous V with curl V.grad S = 0, global rank and local
A2 of abs(S)^beta is 0. The proof builds a weighted potential psi with grad psi = Y/b for the core field Y; psi changes
by a constant gamma t under the twisted scaling, the weighted energy near 0 is O(eps^(2-p)), so gamma = 0 for p < 2,
and psi is constant. (4) V = 0 gives U = 0 as in step (4) of Theorem AX (A570).

Hypotheses beyond the problem: global zero helicity (H9), DU = O(r^(1/2)) (H3), and two premises of type H9: exterior
density of the original vorticity or exterior analyticity, and the A2 property of abs(S)^beta (or S = 0). The A2
property holds if every zero of S lies in a C^1 surface or curve chart with abs(S) comparable to dist^m and m beta
below the codimension, or in a transverse product chart with each m_i beta < 1 (A593-A594); since beta < 1/6 in the
target range, every such zero of order at most 6 qualifies. Neither premise is derived from the target class. Local
analysis cannot supply the A2 premise: for every p > 1, omega and N >= 1 there are real-analytic nonaxisymmetric
equatorial-band germs with all local tail equations and S = g eta^(2N), g > 0, at a point where V and curl V are
nonzero, so abs(S)^beta is not A2 there once 2N beta >= 1 (the literature audit LIT155, A599; local only, without pole regularity or
the canonical global pressure). Analyticity of U does not give analyticity or nodal control of S. The restriction
p < 2 in step (3) is sharp for the standalone tail theorem: at c = 1/3 the punctured radial field V = Qx/abs(x)^3,
P2 = -Q^2/(2 abs(x)^4), satisfies the other hypotheses with global A2 but carries a point charge at 0 (the literature audit LIT156,
A600; outside the target interval). With rank only on {curl V != 0} and the A2 property, k and S are nonzero wherever
curl V != 0, and grad k = 0 forces V = 0 (A597). Contrapositive: a nonzero helicity-free profile with
DU = O(r^(1/2)) in 2/5 < c < 1/2 has (i) a nonzero tail scalar S for which abs(S)^beta is not locally A2 (by A593-A594
this needs a zero of S without such a chart, for instance one of order m >= 1/beta > 6 across a surface, or a flat
zero), or (ii) open irrotational sets of U meeting every exterior region, with U real-analytic on no exterior
region.

Remark (synthesis combination CO34, CONFIRMED [A603-A604]; as summarized in the accompanying artifacts). Premise (a) can be
replaced by density of the tail vorticity {curl V != 0} in R^3 minus 0: the tail rank on {curl V != 0} (the limit of
A413, as in A534 and A556) extends to global rank by continuity of grad k and grad S. The two density premises are in
fact equivalent: A603 (CONFIRMED; for C^2/C^1 profiles with 1/3 < c < 1, bounded U with vanishing blow-down and Dini
DU, supplied by the natural bounds or by U -> 0 with A601) shows that original vorticity density in one exterior
region, density on the escaping set, density everywhere and tail vorticity density are equivalent, by the exact
identity W(Xi x) = D Xi(x) Omega(x) for the scattering map Xi. So, if abs(S)^beta is locally A2, a nonzero profile in
the class has a nonempty open twisted invariant set Sigma_0 = {grad k x grad S != 0} contained in {curl V = 0}; on it
V = -grad k/a, k and P2 + abs(V)^2/2 are harmonic and grad S is not parallel to V; and some ball O inside Sigma_0 has
curl U = 0 on the union of the e^(tA)O, t >= t0, an actual irrotational spiral region of U (A604, CONFIRMED). Excluding
such a cone is the remaining tail question under the A2 premise. Local analysis does not exclude it: the literature audit LIT157
(A607, CONFIRMED as an exact local countertest) gives an analytic irrotational cone with all local equations, S < 0,
local A2 and rank zero on an interface but not next to it, and the literature audit LIT158 (A617, CONFIRMED only as a local countertest;
its full radial momentum residual is nonzero, so it is not a profile) a matched local C^(1,1) band with an irrotational
and a vortical side. Synthesis CO36 (CONFIRMED [A625-A627]; as summarized in the accompanying artifacts, from the second-model review summarized in the accompanying artifacts): k = r^(1-p) kappa on Sigma_0 with kappa annihilated by an elliptic operator on S^2 with negative
zeroth-order coefficient (1-p)(2-p), so if k = 0 on the boundary of a component of int{curl V = 0}, then V = 0 on it;
hence every component of int{curl V = 0} containing a rank failure point has a boundary point where k != 0. A625
confirms this for every C^1 divergence-free homogeneous V with 1 < p < 2 and every omega, with no helicity, pressure or
boundary regularity used. The interface is a transmission problem that local data do not close: on an interface piece
with k != 0, S = D abs(k)^(1/eta) with matching gradient, but S - D abs(k)^(1/eta) is not harmonic on the irrotational
side, so the Cauchy data of the harmonic pair (k, Pi) do not continue the rank (A626); analytic local band germs with
k = 0, curl V nowhere 0 and S <= 0 vanishing to any even order exist (A627, local tail equations only). Synthesis
CO38 (CONFIRMED [A651-A652]; as summarized in the accompanying artifacts, from the second-model review) is the converse side: if the rank holds on a
component Sigma of int{curl V = 0} with V != 0 on Sigma, then S = D abs(k)^(1/eta) on Sigma with D < 0 and
r^(p-1) abs(k) is bounded below on Sigma (from Laplacian S = -(2/a^2) abs(D^2 k)^2 and the homogeneity bound
abs(D^2 k) >= (1-c) abs(grad k)/abs(Ax)), so k and S have no zero on its closure; hence a nonzero component whose
closure meets {k = 0} or {S = 0} has rank failure. Only div V = 0, (T3) and homogeneity are used. A652: if S has no
zero and int{curl V = 0} is a single component with C^1 boundary, a cap gives V = 0 and a band forces opposite
boundary constants and rank failure in the band. Neither incidence of {k = 0} with such a closure nor the rank in
general follows.

Nonvanishing tail scalar (synthesis CO35, check of the second-model review, CONFIRMED [A618-A621];
as summarized in the accompanying artifacts).
If S has no zero on R^3 minus 0, then in the coordinates rho = log r, z = cos theta, chi = phi + t log r (t = omega/c),
with V.dx = r^(1-p)(K d rho + gamma), gamma a one-form on S^2, S = r^(-2p) h and f = abs(h)^beta, a global identity
on S^2, D + (p-1)(2-p) int abs(K) = t (2-p) int (abs(K)/f + (p-1) Psi) d_chi f with D >= 0 and Psi a Lipschitz
potential built from gamma, K and f, uses only (T1), (T4) and the rank on
{curl V != 0}, and includes the irrotational region. So for omega = 0, or for S axisymmetric about the rotation axis,
K = 0, and then an elliptic equation on S^2 gives V = 0: the profile is zero with no density premise and no symmetry of
V. The same holds for any omega if the angular components of V are trigonometric polynomials of degree at most 3 in chi.
Kinematic part: every nonzero divergence-free twisted homogeneous field of degree -p, 1 < p < 2, with V.curl V = 0 has a
zero of k, because curl(V/k) = 0 where k != 0 and a potential of V/k would give a compact surface with nonzero flux
(A620, every omega, no pressure). A621 confirms the exact reductions of the remaining cases (zeros of S, and S < 0 with
an irrotational region) as equivalent systems; their solvability is OPEN, and the general twist term has no known
sign. The omega = 0 conclusions are tail-level checks only: omega = 0 is already settled by the nonrotating theorem
(A010).

Low pressure multipoles (spectral analysis C40, the literature audit LIT159-LIT160; A608-A613 and A622-A624, CONFIRMED). For a profile in the
helicity-free class with DU = O(r^(1/2)) (or the natural bounds), every low far-field multipole Theta_n of the actual
pressure with (n+5)c < 3 vanishes, for every omega, with no density premise and no A2 premise on S (A623; the
borderline n = 2 at c = 3/7 is not included). Ingredients: coefficient-independent A2 bounds for polynomial weights
(A608); weighted rigidity for any homogeneous transported scalar of degree -nu, nu > a (A609); transport and rank
inherited by every low multipole, with at most one degree or rotational pair surviving (A610-A611); and the symmetry
transfer LIT160: an axisymmetric transported scalar with locally integrable inverse weight forces V to be axisymmetric
(A622). Consequences: if the actual S is axisymmetric about the rotation axis and abs(S)^(-beta) is locally integrable,
then U = 0 (A624; this extends the zero-free case of CO35 to nodal S); and the selected vortical witness of Theorem HF
has rho = -2(1-c) or rho <= -(3-2c) (A612, item 1e). No low moment is forced to be nonzero, so a nonzero profile lies
in the class where all low multipoles vanish; that class is OPEN. The literature audit LIT161 (A635, CONFIRMED) shows for ordinary
homogeneity (omega = 0) and 1 < p < 2 that a C^1 divergence-free field with curl V = 0 wherever x.V = 0 is zero (a
flow on S^2 that preserves {x.V > 0} and expands area); the same statement with k in place of x.V is false for
omega != 0 (A637, the pure swirl below). Its twisted
form is synthesis CO37 (CONFIRMED [A641-A644]; as summarized in the accompanying artifacts, from the second-model review): if
curl V = 0 at every zero of k (which the A2 premise gives, A597), then int_{K>0} R <= 0 <= int_{K<0} R on S^2, that
is int abs(K) <= -t int sgn(K) F, because the quotient field M gamma + tKZ on S^2 has divergence -(2-p)R and crosses
{K = 0} only from {K > 0} to {K < 0}; in 3D, V leaves the cone {k > 0} through its whole lateral boundary (A641: the flux statement is for a complete
outward-oriented graph section of the spiral rays). For
omega = 0 this gives V = 0; for omega != 0 a nonzero tail of this kind must have swirl correlated with sgn K against
the twist, -t int sgn(K) F >= int abs(K) > 0. This is the CO35 identity in inequality form with the zero-free premise
replaced by A2. It is sharp at the kinematic level: the pure swirl rho_c^2 r^(-p-3) Jx (rho_c the distance to the axis)
satisfies its premise with equality and is not zero (the literature audit LIT162 section 6, a negative control), so the pressure and
scalar conditions must enter. A642: with the nodal premise and locally integrable abs(h)^(-eta), h axisymmetric about the
rotation axis gives V = 0 for every omega; A643: a local A2 band shows that the separated defect integral of CO35 can
diverge at zeros of S, so that argument does not pass through nodes unchanged; A644: the pressure mean gives
int abs(K) <= abs(t) (16 pi p (-int h)/(3(p+1)))^(1/2) and V = 0 when int h = 0, but no small-twist threshold.
The literature audit LIT162 (A636, CONFIRMED) extends the finite-mode case of CO35 to A2 nodal S: chi-degree at most N with eta not in
{j/m : 1 <= j <= N, 1 <= m <= 2N} gives U = 0 under A2, with no density or zero-free premise (N <= 3 throughout the
target interval). The literature audit LIT163 (A639) extends the symmetry transfer A622 by an angular energy argument (every omega
for 1/4 < c < 1/2); it excludes no class beyond A623-A624. spectral analysis C41 (A638): in a hypothetical nonzero low-multipole
band, full rank forces V = 0, otherwise the band contains an open invariant irrotational rank-failure set; for actual
profiles this is superseded by A623. Under the nodal premise, what remains for omega != 0 is to exclude invariant
probabilities nu of the quotient field on Lambda_+ (the intersection over s >= 0 of the backward images of
closure{K > 0}) with int R dnu <= 0, that is t int F dnu <= -int K dnu (a signed swirl correlation with a latitude
weight; azimuthal winding is not implied), and to handle the zeros of V. The auditor A645 confirms this form: if {K > 0} is
nonempty, such a nu exists, and it may be a point mass on {V = 0}; equivalently, no C^1 weight psi > 0 satisfies
(2-p) psi R - Bq.grad psi > 0 near Lambda_+. This is the sharpest current form of the remaining tail
problem for omega != 0. The literature audit LIT164 (A649, CONFIRMED): at p = 5/4 the same pure swirl has an explicit canonical pressure with
S < 0 everywhere, so canonical pressure, S < 0, A2, zero helicity and the nodal premise together still allow equality in
CO37; its W.grad S and rank defects are nonzero, so (T4) and (T5) must be used. The literature audit LIT165 (A647-A648, CONFIRMED) derives a
second transported scalar of the actual tail from the first pressure correction p1 of A575 (c != 3/7, every omega, no
density or A2, using A623): tau = p1 - 2V.grad P2, of twisted degree -(3-2c), C^(1,alpha), with W.grad tau = 0 on D and
grad k x grad tau = 0 on {W != 0}. So every interface of a rank-failing irrotational component carries a second
matching condition from the vortical side, tau = E abs(k)^((3-2c)/(1-2c)) beside S = D abs(k)^(1/eta) (synthesis
reading). The literature audit LIT166 (A650, CONFIRMED) applies it to the LIT158 matched interface (A617): its analytic vortical germ
admits no p1 with the twisted scaling, -Delta p1 = 2 tr(DV DZ) and the LIT165 rank, for every 0 < p - 1 < 1/2 and
every omega (the quadratic residual is an explicit nonzero rational function of p), so that germ is not the actual
tail of a profile in the LIT165 class (c != 3/7). This rejects one germ, not every interface; A646 records the focused
independent comparison that proposed the test. The literature audit LIT167-LIT168 (A653-A655, CONFIRMED) remove the exception c = 3/7: the exact renormalized moment
allows a logarithm and finitely many periodic harmonic modes, and all of them vanish by the phasewise rank and transport
identities with A622 and A570, so under Theorem HF and the natural bounds the unaveraged next scalar exists for every c in
the target range and every finite omega, and A650 excludes the specified germ also at c = 3/7. The literature audit LIT169 (CONFIRMED [A670-A672]) extends the A650 test from the
pressure level D = 1 to every real level D in the normalized equatorial family (axisymmetric, swirl-free, zero polar
and nonzero radial velocity at the equator; D = d/(2(d+1)) has no analytic leading solution): no C^1 p1 on a positive
band has the scaling, the Poisson equation and the tau rank, by two exact resultants whose gcd has no zero in
0 < d < 1/2 (A672: the first two coefficients alone leave genuinely vortical surviving levels, so all four are
needed). The literature audit LIT170 (CONFIRMED [A676]) removes the analyticity and parity premises: C^1 velocity, C^2 pressure, local
axisymmetry without swirl, nonzero radial interface velocity and zero interface vorticity force this family. General
transmission remains OPEN. The literature audit LIT172 (CONFIRMED [A926-A927]; A928 OPEN): in the same local class with arbitrary polar interface amplitude b, the C^1 velocity and C^2 pressure hypotheses exclude the level D = 1/q (the residual is a strictly positive sum of squares) and force a unique analytic one-sided germ for every nonpolar latitude and every omega (A926); the next transported scalar p1 is analytic on the band (A927); no exclusion of general interfaces follows (A928 OPEN). The literature audit LIT171 (CONFIRMED [A929-A931]; A932 OPEN) settles radial interface data at every nonpolar latitude: in the local class of LIT170 (C^1 velocity, C^2 pressure, axisymmetric without swirl, twisted homogeneity, the Poisson equation and the rank identity) with radial interface velocity V = lambda e_r, lambda != 0, and zero vorticity at a latitude -1 < h < 1, no C^1 next scalar p1 with its scaling, Poisson equation and rank identity exists, for every omega and both signs of lambda (A931; four exact next-pressure coefficients [A929] and an exact resultant elimination whose degree-18 residual factor is strictly positive on 0 < d < 1/2 [A930]). The actual-profile application needs global zero helicity, the natural rates and an adjacent vortical band; general polar interface velocity, swirl, nonaxisymmetric interfaces, poles and zero radial amplitude remain OPEN (A932). An independent derivation (synthesis check of the second-model review,
as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A661-A664] as synthesis CO40) gives the same constant and polynomial, shows that a nonhomogeneous local p1
does not rescue the germ, and gives on every vortical patch with k != 0 the closed form p1 = 2V.grad P2 + gamma abs(k)^nu,
nu = (3p+1)/(p-1), so the remaining local condition is the Poisson equation for this p1 (A662: the other transport identity is then
automatic; on irrotational patches only Delta(p1 + V.Z) = 0 holds, with no rank; A663: at regular vortical zeros of k,
S1 = O(abs(k)^(q-1)) and p1 = V.Z; nothing is claimed at critical zeros). spectral analysis C42 (CONFIRMED [A665-A666]): for a
C^1 divergence-free helicity-free twisted field (1/3 < c < 1/2, every omega), curl(V/k) = 0 on {k != 0} and no
component of {k != 0} carries a potential of cV/k tending to +infinity at its whole boundary (the weak form of the
A620 flux argument); if S < 0 on R^3 minus 0, every component of {k != 0} contains two vortical components with
different constants k/(c abs(S)^eta), and, if these constants are bounded away from 0 on it (for instance if it
contains only finitely many vortical components), a loop with a nonzero period of V/k (revised 09:54Z after its
referee; no nonzero pure swirl admits such an S). For the pure swirl this period is -2 pi/omega around the axis,
which is where the rotation enters. The auditor A667-A669 (CONFIRMED) strengthen this: with S zero-free and the same rank
and transport hypotheses, grad h x grad theta = 0 everywhere (h = abs(S)^(-eta) k/c, c grad theta = abs(S)^(-eta)
(Ax) x curl V), so phi(h) grad theta is a global closed form and every period of V/k is 0. Hence every nonempty
k-sign component has infinitely many vortical components whose constants tend to 0, accumulating at a boundary point
where V, curl V and k vanish; the finite-component case is impossible, and the pure swirl admits no zero-free S for
any omega (no pressure used). A669 checks a staircase only as a scalar model. The infinite-component case is OPEN.
Synthesis CO39 (CONFIRMED [A677-A681] with scope qualifications; as summarized in the accompanying artifacts, from the second-model review), under the nodal premise
{k = 0} in {curl V = 0}, every omega: (i) if K is one-signed, then V = DV = 0 on the zero cone of k (a nonzero DV
would make the zero a hyperbolic saddle of the field X with i_X dA = gamma, and the inverse-integrating-factor equation
XK = K div X would force K = 0 on its stable separatrix) and S = P2 = 0 on the twisted rays over the boundary of
{K = 0} (a Hopf barrier lemma for u = -K, valid however the constants of S = C_j abs(k)^q behave on accumulating
components); (ii) hence, with zero-free S, a nonzero tail cannot have one-signed K; (iii) the CO37 inequality is an

1e. Necessary witnesses for a nonzero helicity-free profile (CONDITIONAL on global zero helicity, a necessary-structure
theorem, the auditor A571
CONFIRMED; synthesis assembly CO31, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts). This is not a nonexistence result.

Theorem HF. Let 2/5 < c < 1/2, omega real, and let U in C^2, P in C^1 solve div U = 0 and the profile equation, with
U.curl U = 0 everywhere and U(y) -> 0 uniformly, U not identically 0. Write B = Ay + U, Omega = curl U, a = 1 - 2c.
Then some connected component E of {Omega != 0} has Gamma_E >= 2a (Gamma_E the largest backward Lyapunov exponent of
ergodic probabilities on Z_E = K cap closure(E) cap ({B = 0} cup {Omega = 0}), K the absorbing core of the backward
carrier flow; A430, A484), and Z_E contains one of:
(W1v) a vortical carrier equilibrium q != 0 with U(q) != 0, spec DB(q) = {rho, 1+c, -a - rho}, rho <= -2a; under the
      derivative bound DU = O(r^(1/2)), rho = -2(1-c) or rho <= -(3-2c) (A612: the resonant rates -(k+3)c of A551
      are excluded for every omega, and every low pressure multipole vanishes);
(W1i) an irrotational carrier equilibrium q != 0 with U(q) != 0 and min Re spec DB(q) <= -2a; if D Omega(q) != 0, the
      first spectral family with rho >= a/2 and a regular box, or rho <= -2a with vortical points of the level
      {H = H(q)} accumulating at q (rho <= -2(1-c) under the derivative bound), or rho <= -2a with Omega = 0 on that
      level near q (as summarized in the accompanying artifacts lists the exact forms);
(W2)  a flat periodic carrier orbit (Omega = D Omega = 0, U != 0 and U.B = 0 on it, constant covector rate rho,
      Floquet multipliers 1, e^(rho T), e^((3c - rho)T)) with rho <= -2a or rho >= 2 - c, and the cylinder properties of
      A474, A523 and A537.
Contrapositive: if no Z_E contains such an object, U = 0.

Proof: assembly of A432 (componentwise Liouville theorem), A430 and A484 (attainment), A467 and A470-A471
(classification of the selected ergodic measure), A468-A469, A478, A496, A518, A551 (equilibrium spectra and rates),
A522, A537 (irrotational cases), A474, A523, A537 (flat periodic orbits); written out as summarized in the accompanying artifacts
and independently reconstructed in A571.

### B.4 Every omega? (historical section 4)

The results in 1a-1e hold for every omega, including the conditional Theorems AX and DA (item 1d) and the
witness Theorem HF (item 1e), whose periodic witness (W2) needs omega != 0 (A030, A587). What is known about how omega enters (spectral analysis; text from
as summarized in the accompanying artifacts, every statement with its verdict):

(4a) Omega-blindness (A043). Applying the derivative of a rotation-equivariant local density Q(U) to (E) and
integrating against an axisymmetric weight gives literally the omega = 0 identity; this covers energy, helicity,
enstrophy and angular-momentum identities with radial or axisymmetric weights. Quantities that depend on P or on omega
explicitly, and the pressure torque d_theta P, are not covered. One quadratic balance in which omega survives is
omega int phi abs(LU)^2 = int phi LU.[c(y.grad)U + (U.grad)U + grad P] for axisymmetric phi, where LU = (Jy.grad)U - JU is the vector rotation generator (A1283; the Cartesian componentwise reading is REFUTED, A1284); it
has no sign, and its linear part is saturated by log-spiral tails. It is not the only one: densities that are not
rotation-equivariant also retain omega. For example, pairing the first Cartesian component of (E) with phi U_1 gives
omega int phi U_1 U_2 = int ((1 - 5c/2) phi - (c/2) y.grad phi) U_1^2 + int phi U_1 ((U.grad)U_1 + d_1 P) for
axisymmetric compactly supported phi (A382, which REFUTES the earlier unrestricted uniqueness wording; A043 itself is
unaffected because U_1^2 is not equivariant).

(4b) Rigidity of the rate and trivial linear kernel (A046). For 0 < c < 1/2 a nonzero C^2 decaying profile solves (E)
for at most one omega. For every c > 0 and every omega the linearization at U = 0 has no nonzero C^2 decaying
solution. Neither statement is a spectral gap: for the mode-m ray symbol sigma_m(lambda) = (1-c) + c lambda - i m omega of
the scalar velocity transport part, and any weight b, inf over real gamma of abs(sigma_m(-b + i gamma)) equals
c abs(alpha - b), alpha = (1-c)/c, for every m and every omega. The roots lie on the critical line Re lambda = -alpha,
and rotation moves them along that line and never off it (A077; weight notation corrected in A384). This concerns the
scalar transport symbol, not the full system with the pressure and the divergence constraint.

(4c) No nonconstant local Lyapunov function on admissible jets for omega != 0 (A044, A081, A100; local
realization of admissible jets A090; wording A2744-A2745). For
omega != 0, a C^1 function of the jet (y, U, DU, D^2 U, P) that is nonincreasing along B at every admissible jet is
constant on admissible jets; for omega = 0 it is a nondecreasing function of H_0 = H - c(1-2c)abs(y)^2/2
(A2177-A2178). At order k >= 5 the literal statement
over all admissible jets is false, but the counterexample is supported at stagnating jets outside the closure of
solution jets and vanishes on every local solution (spectral analysis C28; A345-A347). On the closure of nonstagnating
admissible jets the classification holds at order three (spectral analysis C31; A434): for 0 < c < 1/2 and every omega, a C^1
function of the velocity 3-jet and the pressure value that is nonincreasing along B at every nonstagnating
admissible 4-jet equals, on the closure of the nonstagnating admissible 3-jets and hence on every local C^3 solution
with P in C^1, a constant if omega != 0 and a nondecreasing C^1 function of H_0 if omega = 0. The same holds at order
four (spectral analysis C33; A489, CONFIRMED at the universal-jet scope; synthesis review as summarized in the accompanying artifacts): a
C^1 function of the velocity 4-jet and the pressure value that is nonincreasing along B at every nonstagnating
admissible 5-jet equals, on the closure of the nonstagnating admissible 4-jets and hence on every local C^4 solution,
a constant if omega != 0 and a nondecreasing function of H_0 if omega = 0. The same holds at order five (spectral analysis C34;
A493, CONFIRMED at the universal-jet and closure(N5) scope). It is UNRESOLVED for k >= 6. So for omega != 0 a
monotone quantity cannot be a C^1 function of the jet through order five. Local functions of jets of order >= 6 are
not excluded while that classification is open (A384). This is a method obstruction only; it
restricts no invariant set or witness.

(4d) Far field (A075, A077; one wording REFUTED, A076; one consequence CONDITIONAL, A079). In the twisted gauge
V(y) = R(beta)U(R(-beta)y) with beta = (omega/c) log rho, omega leaves the linear transport part (1-c)V + cDV but
stays in the divergence constraint, the pressure gradient and the quadratic term. For c != 1/3 and every omega,
leading tails rho^(-alpha) F(phi, theta + (omega/c) log rho) are in bijection with smooth tangential fields on S^2:
arbitrary smooth tangential angular data determine a divergence-free leading tail. The leading modal energies E_m are
constrained only by smoothness and reality, sum_m abs(m)^(2N) E_m < infinity for every N and E_(-m) = E_m (A383, which
REFUTES the earlier wording "every distribution of the leading Fourier energy"). No nonlinear extension of such data
is asserted. If omega != 0 and the tail has this form uniformly, the blow-up-time profile is discretely self-similar
with factor e^(2 pi c/abs(omega)) (A079, CONDITIONAL on that tail form). For omega = 0 the conditional terminal field
is continuously homogeneous (A384).

(4e) Torque balance on invariant measures (A107, A238). With X = cy + U and Gamma = (Jy).U, every compactly
supported B-invariant Borel probability mu satisfies int abs(X)^2 dmu = omega int Gamma dmu and
omega int d_theta P dmu = -(1-2c) int abs(X)^2 dmu <= 0. If mu is also rotation-invariant and omega != 0, it is
carried by zeros of B on the axis and by horizontal circles centred on the axis on which U = -cy. These relations
have a sign, but orbits that wind against omega satisfy them, so they exclude no case.

(4f) Perturbative and endpoint results. Near omega = 0 and near axisymmetry (CO8, A093; strengthened by LIT21,
A102): for c in a compact subinterval of (0,1/2) and a global C^{1,alpha} bound there is epsilon > 0 such that
abs(omega) sup abs(LU)/(1+abs(y)) <= epsilon forces U constant (U = 0 under decay); epsilon is not computed. At
c = 2/5 with a globally bounded gradient, U = 0 for every omega (A103).

Reading: the audited kinematic packages and the local low-order identities have not supplied an omega-uniform
obstruction in 2/5 < c < 1/2. This is a statement about the results found, not a classification of possible
obstructions (A384); section 6 gives the precise scope of the kinematic countermodels.

### B.5 Non-axisymmetric profiles? (historical section 5)

Profiles axisymmetric about the rotation axis reduce to omega = 0, because (Jy).grad U = JU cancels the rotation
terms, and are excluded by A010 (the cancellation is the last step of A046; an axisymmetric pressure gives U_theta = 0
by A034 and, for 0 < c < 1/2 and uniformly sublinear U, U = b e_z by A3029, the literature audit LIT359, Theorem AP, also for U, P
in C^1 by A3047, the literature audit LIT364; symmetry of P on one absorbing ball suffices, A3033, the literature audit LIT360, and so does
axisymmetry of the pressure source tr((DU)^2) under E(R) = o(R^3), in particular for decaying profiles, A3040, the literature audit
LIT361 (without that condition a constant horizontal U = b with its affine pressure is a counterexample to the
inference, A3066); whether decay forces an axisymmetric pressure is OPEN, A3031, A3035, A3043, A3049). For C-infinity
decaying profiles the non-axisymmetric problem is reduced by 1c(ii)-(iii) to essential basins with sign-changing
helicity (A309, A327). The following restrictions hold for every c > 0 and every omega under H0, H1 unless stated;
they restrict a hypothetical solution and are not nonexistence results. S denotes the set of m with nonzero angular
mode U~_m. The mode equations behind (5a)-(5c), the linear kernel of (4b) and the torque formula of (5c) were
rechecked in full for every finite omega in A3023 (the auditor review
the accompanying artifacts; the spectral analysis comparison CONFIRMED with its diagnostic limits,
A3024): the local mode equations need no decay, the kernel and support statements use decay, and the torque formula
uses 0 < c < 1/2 and boundedness or uniform sublinearity. The inclusion S in S + S is automatic when 0 is in S, and no
inverse estimate for the constrained operator, exclusion of every finite support or nonexistence is derived
(A3025 OPEN).

(5a) Angular support rule (A073). For every m in S the mode forcing N_m = sum_{k+l=m} (U~_k.grad)U~_l is not a
gradient. In particular S is contained in S + S, which excludes S = {+-L} and every S contained in L(2Z+1).

(5b) Odd symmetry classes are empty (A074). If sigma in O(3) commutes with J and sigma U(sigma^(-1)y) = -U(y), then
U = 0. Examples: even fields; fields odd under z -> -z in the sense U_h(y_h, -z) = -U_h, U_3(y_h, -z) = U_3; fields
with U_{pi/L} = -U, where U_a(y) = R(a)U(R(-a)y).

(5c) Angular mean (A032, A034, A078; under H0 and U = o(abs(y)), for 0 < c < 1/2: A1285; the past torque
representation fails at c = 1/2 and diverges for c > 1/2, A1286). The angular mean solves the omega-free
axisymmetric system with Reynolds forcing. Its angular momentum is the integral of the eddy angular-momentum flux
along the backward orbits of an omega-free field, and Gamma(a) = -int_{-infinity}^0 e^((1-2c)s) (d_theta P)(Y(s; a))
ds along B-orbits, so d_theta P = 0 forces u_theta = 0, and then U = b e_z for 0 < c < 1/2 and uniformly sublinear U
(A3029, Theorem AP). Control of the mean without axisymmetry is UNRESOLVED (the Bernoulli argument of Theorem L2
does not transfer because the Reynolds force has no sign).

(5d) Finite angular spectra (A137, A180, A214). If S is finite with L = max S >= 1, the top mode Z = U~_L solves
the complex steady Euler system (Z.grad)Z + grad Pi_{2L} = 0 on R^3, and for omega != 0 a critical top-mode tail is
never irrotational. Under the derivative decay abs(D^j U) <= C(1+abs(y))^(-alpha-j), j <= 2, and 2/5 < c < 1/2, each
mode energy obeys E_m(R) = L_m R^(5-2/c) + tau_m/(1 - 5c/2) + O(R^(1-alpha)) with sum_m tau_m = 0, and the mode
helicities satisfy (1-2c) H_m = chi_m with sum_m chi_m = 0. For S = {+-1, +-2} the local mode equations allow the
configuration. No mode is forced to vanish.

(5e) Helicity-free profiles without symmetry (Theorem DA, item 1d; A598 and A705-A708, CONDITIONAL). For
2/5 < c < 1/2 and every omega, a helicity-free profile with DU = O(r^(1/2)) is zero if its tail scalar S is 0 or
abs(S)^(-beta) is locally integrable on R^3 minus 0 (no density premise). It is also zero if the nodal premise
{k = 0} in {curl V = 0} holds and V has no zero on S^2 (CO43, A733), or if the joint core K_Omega is empty or S o Xi
is bounded on E intersect B(z, r) for a ball B(z, r) around every point z of K_Omega, E the scattering domain (the literature audit LIT178, A740; quantifier A1211, A1280). No symmetry of U or of its tail is assumed. Nonaxisymmetric tails with all local tail equations exist as local germs (A590, A599); whether one extends
to a global tail with the canonical pressure is OPEN.

The conjecture for non-axisymmetric profiles is UNRESOLVED.

### B.6 Is U -> 0 alone sufficient? (historical section 6)

UNRESOLVED. One related fact is PROVED (Corollary A.5, A406-A407): for every c in (0,1) and every omega, a bounded C^1
profile differs from a decaying-in-the-mean profile only by a constant background b and a shift z0 = -A^{-1}b, and
for 0 < c < 2/5 boundedness alone forces U to be constant. This does not change the target problem: decaying profiles
have b = 0, and the shifted velocity is bounded and therefore uniformly sublinear, but its uniform pointwise decay is not
established by A406 alone, so the results of items 1b-1c that use pointwise decay keep that hypothesis (A503). A second PROVED fact concerns the derivative hypotheses (A476-A477, integral-estimate analysis C35; section 3.1): for
a decaying C^2 profile with 2/5 < c < 1/2, the Dini condition (D), DU -> 0, the strain bound
limsup lambda_max(sym DU) < 1 at infinity and the natural rate abs(DU) = O(abs(y)^(-1/c)) are all equivalent. So the
results conditional on H3 need only DU -> 0. Whether U -> 0 implies DU -> 0 is UNRESOLVED. If it fails, the largest
strain eigenvalue has limsup at least 1 + c/2 as abs(y) -> infinity (A506, CONFIRMED, integral-estimate analysis C40: for bounded U the
limsup of lambda_max(sym DU) is 0 or at least 1 + c/2, and an upper strain bound L gives abs(DU) <= C r^max(0,(L-1)/c)). A prescribed velocity rate raises the threshold: if abs(U) <= C(1+abs(y))^(-k) with k > 0, then
limsup lambda_max(sym DU) < 1 + c min(1,(1+k)/2) already gives DU -> 0 (A520, CONFIRMED, integral-estimate analysis C41); the rate is an extra
hypothesis, not a consequence of U -> 0. The blow-up then has, at time T, a whole twisted ray of
points x_* != 0 at which (T-t) abs(grad u) does not tend to 0 jointly, so its spatial gradient is unbounded near each
of them (A475, A476). No such profile is known, and none is excluded. With U and DU bounded, grad P and DU Ay are
bounded and abs(DU e) + abs(Omega.e) <= C/abs(y) for e = Ay/abs(Ay), with little-o versions when U -> 0 (A485,
CONFIRMED at the bounded-U and bounded-DU scope, integral-estimate analysis C37); this does not give full DU decay. Bounded U and
bounded DU imply Omega = O(1/abs(y)) and DU = O(log abs(y)/abs(y)), hence DU -> 0 and (D), for every omega and
0 < c < 1 (A492, CONFIRMED at the bounded-U and bounded-DU scope; the literature audit LIT120, and independently integral-estimate analysis C39 with the weaker
rate (1 + abs(y))^(-1/8); synthesis review as summarized in the accompanying artifacts); with A476 the rate improves to O(1/abs(y)). So this item reduces exactly to whether U -> 0
forces DU to be bounded. Bounded U and
DU = O(abs(y)^delta) for some delta < 1/3 already force DU bounded (A495, the literature audit LIT122; synthesis review
as summarized in the accompanying artifacts). Bounded U and DU = o(abs(y)^(1/2)), or U -> 0 and DU = O(abs(y)^(1/2)), already force
DU -> 0, for every omega and 0 < c < 1, with no smallness of the constant (A498, CONFIRMED at these two scopes;
The literature audit LIT124-LIT125, synthesis review as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; the earlier one-third result LIT123 is a corollary,
A502). Faster velocity decay buys more gradient growth: if 1/2 < delta < 1, abs(DU) <= C(1+abs(y))^delta and
U = o(abs(y)^(1-2delta)), then grad P = o(abs(y)^(1-2delta)) and DU -> 0, for every omega and 0 < c < 1 (A507,
CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT126, synthesis review as summarized in the accompanying artifacts). The same holds for 1/2 <= delta <= 5/4 with c delta < 1 under DU = O(abs(y)^delta) and U = o(abs(y)^(-(2delta-1))) (A757, CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT127); in 2/5 < c < 1/2 the part delta >= 1/(2c) already follows from the velocity-only energy exclusion A053, so the new content is delta < 1/(2c) (A758). A logarithmic version: DU = O(abs(y)^(1/2)(log abs(y))^gamma) and U = o((log abs(y))^(-2gamma)) give DU -> 0 (A759, CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT128). Neither premise follows from U -> 0. Canonical-pressure decay does not bound gradients: there are smooth divergence-free U in L^2 with canonical P, both tending to 0 uniformly, with DU and grad P unbounded, and with superpolynomial peaks while DU and grad P are in L^3 (A760-A761, CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT129 after the sign repair of A762; kinematic examples, the momentum equation fails for every omega). A small momentum residual does not help either: disjoint smooth swirl tubes give a smooth, rapidly decaying, divergence-free and helicity-free U with its exact canonical pressure, whose momentum residual R satisfies abs(R) <= C eps (1+r)^(-4) uniformly in 0 < c < 1 and omega, with DU and grad P in L^3 and superpolynomial peaks of both (A806-A809, CONFIRMED; the literature audit LIT180). Its residual has unbounded curl, so the example refutes only the inference from an approximate profile equation; it says nothing against theorems on exact profiles (A809). So a decaying profile that fails derivative decay
must have limsup abs(DU)/abs(y)^(1/2) = infinity (A498). This is not a statement that every nonzero profile has fast
gradient growth: nonexistence is not proved even at the bounded-gradient scope (wording CONFIRMED, A501). The pressure
needs no derivative bound: for a C^2 profile with P in C^1, U -> 0 uniformly, 0 < c < 1 and every omega, P equals the
canonical pressure sum_ij d_i d_j Gamma * (U_i U_j) (defined modulo constants by far-kernel subtraction) plus a
constant (A500, CONFIRMED; from the synthesis check as summarized in the accompanying artifacts of an answer of the second-model review, with
independent proofs by the auditor and the literature audit). It does not give pointwise decay of grad P. Since
abs(DU)_F^2 = abs(Omega)^2 - Laplacian P, that is the question whether U -> 0 keeps abs(Omega)^2 - Laplacian P bounded
at infinity. A synthesis-checked construction (second-model review, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; A505, CONFIRMED as an
approximate, non-profile construction) shows that this is not settled by the following estimates. It is a smooth divergence-free field with U -> 0,
Omega -> 0 and an exact Newtonian pressure, so -Laplacian P = tr(DU^2) holds exactly. All the directional limits of
A485 hold, and the momentum residual tends to 0 uniformly. Yet DU = diag(lambda, -lambda, 0) along a whole outgoing
orbit, for any lambda >= 1. Its residual has a derivative that does not tend to 0, so it is not a profile. A proof that U -> 0 forces derivative
decay must therefore use more of the exact equation than these estimates and a vanishing residual; A505 does not
identify which part. Two scalar criteria give DU -> 0 for bounded U, every omega and 0 < c < 1 (A504, CONFIRMED):
limsup(abs(Omega)^2/2 - Laplacian P) < 3/2, improved to (3/2)(1 + c/2)^2 by A506, and
limsup(sqrt((-Laplacian P)_+/2) + abs(Omega)^2/4) < infinity. Neither is derived from U -> 0.
A specific kinematic package does not decide the question of this item: div B = 3c with U smooth and compactly supported, a
nonzero divergence-free W with [B, W] = -(1+c)W on R^3 with the stated decay and regularity, and W nowhere zero
and contracting on a trapping genus-two handlebody of the backward flow. CO6 realizes this package (A066; W
C-infinity by A121) with W different from curl U; its return quotient is expanding with a Lorenz-type local
structure, and for its original parameters no transitive attractor or attractor classification is asserted (a parameter
variant with a transitive attractor follows below). This concerns that package, not
every possible kinematic argument. The regular case (alpha*) is also kinematically realizable (PROVED, A242-A243,
as a deduction from a published surface classification theorem; the literature audit LIT48): for every 0 < c < 1/2 and every omega
there are a compactly supported smooth divergence-free U and a smooth nowhere-zero divergence-free W with
abs(D^j W) = O(abs(y)^(-1/c-j)) and [B, W] = -(1+c)W on R^3, such that the backward flow of B = (cI - omega J)y + U
has a transitive uniformly hyperbolic two-dimensional attractor with exponents -(1+c), 0, 1-2c (entropy 1-2c), W
spans its strong stable line, and its basin is R^3 minus one proper line; the only zero of B has spectrum
{1+c, -(1-2c)/2, -(1-2c)/2}. W is not curl U. The construction combines a smooth surface triple obtained by blowing
up an unstable leaf of the cat map (A233), its exact suspension on the figure-eight knot exterior (A204, A234), the
Yang-Yu classification (arXiv:2004.08921v1, Proposition 4.13) to mark a compact boundary leaf as a meridian (A242),
the transverse-meridian lemma (A183) and the completion to R^3 (CO15, A181). A second proof of the meridian step that
does not use the classification theorem: the Dehn filling along the explicit boundary leaf traced by a prong of the
source has trivial fundamental group, by a word computation for the cat map, with the collapse to the linear model
by Lacher's cell-like mapping theorem and the three-dimensional Poincare theorem (CO19, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts;
PROVED, A246, with the auditor's regular-neighbourhood repair for the punctured-arc inclusion). Consequence: the kinematic identities with decay cannot exclude (alpha*), and an
exclusion needs a property the model lacks, such as W = curl U (A2745; A2742 REFUTED the earlier wording).
For this particular model the Euler coupling does fail: it has no nonzero decaying
first integral of W, and for 2/5 < c < 1/2 no nonzero multiple of the Biot-Savart reconstruction of W is an Euler
profile (LIT49, PROVED, A244-A245). That excludes one reconstruction of one model, not regular attractors of a
general profile.
Case (beta) is kinematically realizable in the target range as well (PROVED, A252-A253; dynamical analysis B24, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts).
Put c_0 = 2(2 - sqrt 2)/(5 - sqrt 2) = 0.3266... For every c_0 < c < 1/2 and every omega, a parameter variant of CO6 (return
parameter K = 1 + sqrt 2/(2q), q = (1 - c/2)/(2 - 5c/2), with all construction inequalities rechecked exactly) gives smooth
compactly supported divergence-free U and a smooth divergence-free W with [B, W] = -(1+c)W on R^3 and W = O(abs(y)^(-1/c)),
and a smooth genus-two handlebody H, strictly trapping for the backward flow, with W nowhere zero near H. The maximal
invariant set of H is a transitive singular-hyperbolic attractor that contains a zero p of B and nonstationary orbits; it
carries a unique physical probability of full support, and Lebesgue-almost every point of H has it as backward limit set.
The proof uses the expanding Lorenz quotient (slope greater than sqrt 2 after normalization, Williams' eventual-onto
argument) and the published singular-hyperbolic attractor theorems of Araujo, Pacifico, Pujals and Viana. W is not curl U,
and the Euler pressure and circulation laws are not imposed. For c <= c_0, outside the target range, this realization is
open. For 2/5 < c < 1/2 and every omega, no nonzero scalar multiple of the Biot-Savart reconstruction of this W is an
Euler profile (the literature audit LIT54, PROVED, A262; for this construction only).

Vortex lines and orbitwise arguments (integral-estimate analysis C36, C43, C44; A579-A586). (a) Along a material vortex segment of a
bounded profile (0 < c < 1, every omega), the stretching integral equals [U.xi] at the ends minus the integral of
U.kappa n, and the length satisfies e^(cs)(L_0 - E) <= L(s) <= e^(cs)(L_0 + E) with E = int_0^s e^(-c tau)(2 + K)M d tau
(K the total curvature, M the velocity bound); so the vorticity decays at the natural rate along a segment as long as
its total curvature and the logarithmic oscillation of abs(Omega) along it stay bounded, with constants from the
initial segment (A579, CONFIRMED). If the curvature grows at most like exp((1 + c + c theta)s) with theta < 1/2, the
initial segments are uniform, the logarithmic oscillation of Omega is bounded and its local Holder seminorms grow at
most polynomially, then DU -> 0 and abs(Omega) + abs(DU) <= C/(1+r) (A580, CONFIRMED as a conditional theorem). For
U -> 0 and 2/5 <= c <= 1/2, at a far point where abs(Omega) does not decay over a unit time window, the direction field
xi = Omega/abs(Omega) has sup abs(D xi) >= 1/(100 m(r/2)) on the vortex ribbon of material length 3.9 m(r/2)
(m(R) = sup over abs(z) >= R of abs(U)), or, if that segment does not exist, div xi is unbounded along a finite-length
vortex line (A581, CONFIRMED with these endpoint repairs). None of the geometric hypotheses is derived from U -> 0.
(b) Every harmonic phi gives an exact local profile U = grad phi, P = -(1-2c)phi - U.Ay - abs(U)^2/2, for every c and
omega; phi = (y1^2 - y2^2)y3 and phi = e^(k y3) J_2(k rho) cos(2 theta) have linear and exponential strain along the
outgoing positive y3-axis while abs(U) <= m on shrinking tubes around it (A582, CONFIRMED as local countertests; both
fail global decay, and a decaying irrotational profile on R^3 is zero). So arguments that use only the equation near
one orbit and the smallness of U on shrinking tubes cannot give derivative decay. The harmonic bound
abs(DU) <= 3m/rho on a ball of radius rho on which abs(U) <= m shows that m/rho -> 0 suffices; the source sentence that
a radius bounded below is necessary was REFUTED (A583). Together with A505: exactness near an orbit (C44) and U -> 0
with the Newtonian pressure (A505) are each compatible with persistent strain along an outgoing orbit; a counterexample
needs both. (c) For bounded U and DU, abs(DU(y)) <= C[w*(abs(y)/16)(1 + log abs(y)) + abs(y)^(-1)] with
w*(r) = sup over abs(z) >= r of abs(Omega), and the Dini-type equivalences follow (A584-A585, CONFIRMED with
joint-limsup and non-continuation qualifications). At that scope A492 already gives DU -> 0, so the two remaining
bounded-gradient classes of the source are empty (A586). The question of this item is still whether U -> 0 forces DU
to be bounded.
Small far-field vorticity (integral-estimate analysis C49; as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; independent proof in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A1068-A1074]; A1075 REFUTED a wording; A1076 OPEN). For a bounded C^2 profile, 0 < c < 1 and every omega, if abs(Omega) <= W0 outside a ball, then for 0 < alpha < 1 and gamma > (1 + alpha)W0/alpha, norm(DU(y)) <= K abs(y)^(gamma/c) for large abs(y) (A1071; no derivative bound, velocity decay or pressure is used; the strain kernel has logarithmic coefficient one, A1068, and the transport and barrier steps are A1069-A1070). If moreover U = O(abs(y)^(-kappa)), kappa >= 0, and omega_inf = limsup abs(Omega) < c delta_*/2 with delta_* = min(5/4, 1/c, (1 + kappa)/2), then DU -> 0 and abs(Omega) + norm(DU) = O(1/abs(y)) (A1072). The threshold is c/4 for bounded U and 1/4 under the natural velocity tail with 2/5 < c < 1/2. So a profile with U -> 0 and DU not -> 0 has omega_inf >= c/4, and a bounded field with Omega -> 0 and persistent gradient cannot satisfy the profile vorticity equation (A1074); in physical variables (T-t) times the exterior vorticity supremum has limsup omega_inf (A1073). The source phrase "type-I upper bound" was REFUTED as an inference (A1075; only a type-I-scale lower bound along sequences holds). Nothing is claimed at or above the threshold (A1076).
Blow-up at a gradient concentration (integral-estimate analysis C46; as summarized in the accompanying artifacts, the hour-16 target (T-H3); CONFIRMED [A682-A688]
as stated below, with the method-completeness claims OPEN [A689]). If U is
bounded and DU is unbounded, rescaling at a gradient concentration at its own velocity scale gives a nonconstant
Lipschitz divergence-free limit that is invariant along the orbit direction e up to a constant shear (Lemma BU). Two
exact steady Euler flows, a shear and the strain diag(1, -1, 0)x/4, satisfy every conclusion of Lemma BU (Proposition O),
so these necessary limit conditions at that scale give no contradiction (Proposition O builds limit fields, not
profiles that realize them; whether every proof must use the profile time scale is a method-completeness question and
OPEN, the auditor 10:08Z): the profile terms enter the rescaled equation only with the factor
1/lambda, and a B-orbit crosses a blow-up ball in time o(1/lambda). In vorticity form, U -> 0 and
w(1 + log^+(H/w)) = O(abs(y)^(1/2)), with w and H the supremum and the C^alpha seminorm of curl U on B(y, 3), give
DU -> 0 (Corollary LV, from the classical Lemma LB and A498; the cited natural rates need c > 1/3, which covers the
target range; A686). Further CONFIRMED parts: at a concentration of size lambda at distance abs(z) the Hessian satisfies
sup over B(z, 2m/lambda) of abs(D^2 U) >= lambda^2/(2m) (A683); each connected passage of an orbit through a fixed
rescaled ball changes vorticity by a relative O(R/T) (A685; repeated returns are not bounded); a vorticity bound
abs(curl U) <= C(1 + r)^delta with delta < 1/2 forces the strain branch at any super-half-power concentration, with
log(2 + H(z_n))/abs(z_n)^(1/2 - delta) -> infinity for the Holder seminorm H (A688). Exact text for the obstruction
(A689): the concentration limit can satisfy all the currently derived limiting equations, including the stationary
Euler equations, as the explicit shear and strain show; these conditions alone give no contradiction, and it is open
whether further constraints from the profile equation exclude the limits. No claim is made that a proof must use the
profile time scale or outside information. A690 (CONFIRMED, from the actual manuscript of Gavrilov, arXiv 1810.08020):
smooth stationary Euler fields with U -> 0, finite energy and arbitrarily large prescribed gradients exist (disjoint
scaled copies of the compact Gavrilov flow); they are not profiles, so the steady-Euler part of any blow-up limit cannot
by itself bound DU. The remaining step is stated there as Open Lemma II.
Localized depletion of vortex stretching (integral-estimate analysis C48, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts; CONFIRMED [A902-A907]; A908 REFUTED; A909
OPEN). For U in C^2 divergence-free near B(z, 2 rho) and a unit vector xi with W(z) x xi = 0 (W = curl U; W(z) = 0 is allowed, A944), the strain
satisfies abs(xi.S(z)xi) <= D_rho + 5 log 2 m_ann/rho, where D_rho = (3/(4 pi)) int_{abs(x) < 2 rho} abs(W(z+x) x xi) abs(x)^(-3) dx
measures local misalignment of the vorticity and m_ann is the supremum of abs(U) on the annulus rho <= abs(y - z) <= 2 rho
(A902; no profile equation is used). For decaying C^2 profiles, 0 < c < 1 and every omega, the annular remainder
tends to zero at far points (A903). If the C^alpha seminorm of W on B(y, 3) grows at most polynomially and the
average of D_rho along every backward carrier segment from a far vortical point to a fixed sphere is at most
1 + c/2 - epsilon, then DU tends to zero, and for c > 1/3 (which covers the target range) the natural bounds hold
(A904; no helicity premise). Conversely, vorticity growth abs(W(z_n)) >= delta abs(z_n)^(1/2) forces the segment
average of D_rho to be at least 1 + c/2 - o(1) (A905); under the same polynomial Holder growth, a failure of DU -> 0 gives
far vortical points whose segment averages are at least 1 + c/2 - o(1) (A943, the contrapositive of A904). The transport facts, shell times (A906) and one exact nondecaying
profile with three kinematic tests (A907; none is a decaying counterexample) are confirmed. A908 REFUTES the word
"equivalently" in the source (the positive-part bound is a consequence of the average bound, not equivalent to it).
Whether the averaged misalignment bound follows from decay, and the natural-rate clause for c <= 1/3, are OPEN (A909).
So, under polynomial Holder growth of curl U, a bound of the backward-segment misalignment average by 1 + c/2 - epsilon,
with one epsilon > 0 uniformly on far segments, suffices for the derivative premise (T-H3) (A904; wording A945);
neither the Holder growth nor that bound is derived from decay (A909, A946 OPEN).

### B.7 Status of the main conjecture (historical section 7)

UNRESOLVED (A009 OPEN). For C-infinity profiles the open case is now narrower (item 1c, A308-A309, A317): a nonzero
C-infinity decaying profile must have at least one invariant open essential basin of a vortical SRB measure on which
U.Omega takes both signs, and by A326-A327 it takes both signs on the same Bernoulli level for every level in some
open interval. At C^2, on every open set invariant under the vortex flow, the sets of Bernoulli values attained with
U.Omega > 0 and with U.Omega < 0 are open and agree up to a null set of values (A387, the literature audit LIT76). For C^2 uniformly sublinear profiles, 0 < c < 1/2 and every omega, almost every vortex line either has
U.Omega identically zero or has U.Omega taking both strict signs arbitrarily far in both directions; on almost every
line of the first kind U.B is constant (spectral analysis C30, A348). For real-analytic profiles the first kind is a null set in
every component where U.Omega is not identically zero (A349); analyticity is not derived for profiles. The sign of
the helicity-crossing derivative Omega.grad(U.Omega) is locally free (A350), so a sign-change exclusion cannot come
from jet constraints alone. Whether the zero-helicity lines can fill positive volume in the C^2 or C-infinity class
is UNRESOLVED (A319). Under the Dini hypothesis (D) the far field does not decide the sign question (integral-estimate analysis C31): a
one-signed far field on a basin D forces negative helicity of positive volume, inside a fixed ball, in every open band
of Bernoulli levels on one side of the limit value p_inf (A363), which is the same-level structure of A327 and not a
contradiction; an explicit smooth tail, defined off the origin, has positive helicity for every omega and satisfies
the tail identities (A362); almost every vortical line meets the core in both vortex-time directions, with tail arcs
of finite length (A360). The stronger every-orbit and every-level readings are OPEN (A364); almost every exact
level does follow (A387).
Closure from a gauge sign (integral-estimate analysis C47, CONFIRMED [A852-A859]; A860 REFUTED, A861 OPEN). For 0 < c < 1/2, every omega,
U in C^2, P in C^1, U decaying: if Omega.(U + lambda y + grad f) = 0 outside a compact set for some lambda != 0 and
some f in C^3 with grad f bounded, then U = 0 (Theorem E, A853; no helicity premise and no DU bound; lambda = c, f = 0
is the condition V.Omega = 0 outside a compact set, V = cy + U, due to an second-model review). In the C-infinity
essential-basin class, one sign of Omega.(U + lambda y + grad f) on each essential basin forces U = 0, for lambda = 0,
f = 0 (Theorem 5) and for every lambda != 0, and finiteness of one of the two one-sided integrals of the wrong sign
along almost every vortex orbit suffices (A854); for lambda != 0 the same variation criterion at almost every point of
{Omega != 0} already works at C^2 (A855). Mirror-symmetric profiles (U(Ry) = RU(y), R = diag(1, 1, -1)) in the C^2/C^1
decaying class have Omega = 0 on the mirror plane (A856); in the C-infinity class every essential basin lies in one
half-space and R pairs upper and lower basins, so one sign of U.Omega on each upper basin gives U = 0 (A857); for
omega != 0 the plane reflection is the only improper orthogonal symmetry commuting with the rotation that has a
positive-dimensional fixed set (A858). A860 REFUTES the source sentence that every step of Theorem E survives a
compactly supported scalar gauge replacement (only the Omega = 0 part does; Theorem E for actual profiles stands).
Whether the known null tests exhaust scalar methods, or a field-dependent gauge coincidence can be ruled out, is OPEN
(A861). So the closure from a sign holds for the whole gauge family; the open step is to derive a sign.
At the C^2 baseline, without an additional intrinsic growth condition, neither this reduction nor the coverage step is available (A318). What does hold at C^2 for
uniformly sublinear profiles, 0 < c < 1/2 and every omega: if U.Omega >= 0 everywhere (or <= 0 everywhere), then
U.Omega = 0 identically (A328 with E = R^3 and I = R). So at C^2 the one-signed case of the conjecture is exactly
the helicity-free case. In that case, on the basin of a regular basic hyperbolic backward attractor H is constant
(CO22, B26; A291, A310; concluding U = 0 still needs coverage by such basins), and a compact transitive
singular-hyperbolic backward attractor with the stated domination and a vortical carrier zero cannot have a
helicity-free basin (B29, A366; no coverage needed). The non-dominated and mixed cases are open. C^2 coverage holds under the single
condition Gamma_Z < 2(1-2c) on ergodic probabilities carried by {B = 0} or {Omega = 0} in the core (A398-A399,
A416-A417), and under its weaker componentwise form Gamma_E < 2(1-2c) for each component E of {Omega != 0}
(A430-A431); this condition is not known to follow from decay, and local identities cannot give it (A415, A423). With
coverage, a C^2 helicity-free decaying profile vanishes if {Omega != 0} is dense (A413-A414). Without coverage, a
helicity-free profile with DU = O(r^(1/2)) vanishes if the tail scalar is 0 or abs(S)^(-beta) is locally integrable
(Theorem DA, A598 strengthened by A705-A708, no density premise), or under the nodal premise when V has no zero on
S^2 (CO43, A733), or when the joint core K_Omega is empty (LIT178, A740); no symmetry is assumed, and no premise is
known to follow from decay. Under the same
condition, or its componentwise form, and with no density assumption, one sign of U.Omega on each D_nu forces U = 0
at C^2 (A422, A432); in particular every globally one-signed C^2 decaying profile with Gamma_E < 2(1-2c) for every
component E vanishes. In this helicity-free C^2 class the condition can fail only at a carrier equilibrium atom or on a
flat periodic orbit (Omega = D Omega = 0, U != 0, U.B = 0, constant covector rate rho) with rho <= -2(1-2c) or
rho >= 2 - c: every nonflat nonstationary ergodic probability on {Omega = 0} has top exponent (1-2c)/2 (A433, A467),
and every aperiodic flat one has top exponent 0 (A470-A471). The description that
follows is the C^2 picture. Open case: a positive-measure vortical set with backward limits neither points nor single
periodic orbits; by CO9 (A115) either (alpha*) a regular basic hyperbolic backward attractor exists, or
(beta)/(gamma) a positive-measure set of vortical points has alpha-limits that contain both zeros of B and
nonstationary orbits (limits inside {B = 0} are excluded by A111, A122) or touch {Omega = 0}. In case (alpha*) the
attractor is two-dimensional; being transitive it has a connected trapping neighbourhood N without zeros of B, and
the boundary of N is a single torus (A087, stated per connected component), and a.e. vortex line of its basin crosses
it infinitely often (CO12, A154); both vortex half-lines through each of its points leave the trapping region (B21,
A158); its return maps on vortex-tangent sections have the skew form (F(u), F'(u)^{-(1+c)/(1-2c)} v + G(u)) with return
time log F'/(1-2c) (CO13, A161); and the B-flow outside N has bounded orbits and, since B has no zero in N, a zero of B outside N (CO13,
A162; the bounded-orbit part holds for every compact smooth trapping domain whose boundary is not a single
2-sphere). In case (beta), zeros of B in nonpoint limit sets contained in {Omega != 0} are real saddles
{1+c, lambda_2 >= 0, lambda_3 < 0} (A147, A159; not proved when the limit set meets {Omega = 0})
and finite networks of
hyperbolic vortical zeros have null basins (B20, A155). For an assumed two-branch Lorenz-type return geometry, the
vortex-flux branch law f' = exp((1-2c)T) and the Euler period inequality log (f^n)' >= 2 pi (1-2c)/abs(omega) hold
(B22, A171, A173); these are necessary conditions, not an exclusion. For a constant-roof attractor (constant
return time) with flux slope lambda and least return count n_0, n_0 log lambda >= 2 pi (1-2c)/abs(omega) (dynamical analysis B25,
A279); this does not force lambda to infinity as omega -> 0, because the return count can grow (A280 refutes that
inference). All the (alpha*) properties listed above
are kinematic, and the regular model of item 6 (A243) satisfies them, so excluding (alpha*) requires W = curl U.
The same holds for case (beta) in the target range: the parameter variant of CO6 in item 6 (A252, A253) has a
positive-volume set of points, with W nonzero, whose backward limit set contains a zero of B and nonstationary orbits.
No kinematic model of case (gamma) has been constructed. An independent analysis (the second-model review, answer type
"neither model nor proof"; synthesis check 23:41Z; audited later, A2265-A2270) shows where the natural constructions fail. Write
theta = (B x W).dy. Then curl(B x W) = (1-2c)W and Psi_t^* theta = e^{(1-2c)t} theta, so
abs(DPsi_t(a)) >= e^{(1-2c)t} abs(theta(a))/abs(theta(Psi_t a)), and theta(a) != 0 when W(a) != 0, the positive X-orbit of a is precompact and alpha(a) has no zero of B (A2299).
(a) A multiple f W_0 of a known bracket pair needs B f = 0 and W_0.grad f = 0, so a cutoff cannot create zeros of W in
the limit set of a point where f W_0 != 0, if W_0 has no zero there.
(b) In a globally triangular model X = -B = (F(q), H(q, z)), W = w(q) d_z, q in R^2, the equations
give div(wF) = (1-2c)w, so the planar flow phi_t of F has abs(w(phi_t q)) det Dphi_t(q) = e^{(1-2c)t} abs(w(q)), and no
positive-area set of bounded trajectories with w != 0 exists. (c) If a return section carries coordinates (r, z) in
which W = w(r, z) d_z with fibres extending smoothly across the limiting cycle r = 0 (W itself may vanish there to
infinite order), then theta restricted to the section is h(r) dr, the return map is (f(r), g(r, z)), and in the flux
coordinate s = int_0^r abs(h) it satisfies F'(s) = e^{(1-2c) tau} > 1: the cycle repels on the side r > 0. For monomial
saddle chains X = h_i x d_x - b_i y d_y - a_i z d_z, W = x^{p_i} y^{q_i} d_z the bracket forces
(p_i + 1)h_i - (q_i + 1)b_i = 1 - 2c, which with q_i = p_{i+1} gives prod b_i/h_i < 1. (The identities in (a)-(c) and the
monomial condition are checked symbolically in the accompanying artifacts; the auditor reconstructed the
conclusions independently: the covector identity A2265, (a) A2266, (b) for a global product representation A2267,
(c) for a return extending with F(0) = 0 and smooth transverse fibres A2268, and the monomial chains with cyclic
order matching A2269.) These exclude particular constructions, not case (gamma) (A2270 OPEN): a degenerating
direction field of W at its zeros, a non-smooth fibre structure or a nonhyperbolic zero set are untouched. Its two
other conclusions are already in the record: convergence of vortical points to a single equilibrium happens only on
a null set (Theorem D3(a), A058), and its argument for mixed regular basic attractors is the mechanism of CO20 below.
On an open set O where the bracket holds, the coupling has an exact loop form (spectral analysis C24, PROVED, A249): curl U = W on O
together with a single-valued pressure is equivalent to the identity oint B.dl + 2 omega A_12 = (1/(1-2c)) oint (B x W).dy
for every closed curve in O (A_12 the signed area of the horizontal projection). If curl U = W on O, the pressure is
single-valued if and only if the periods of (1-2c)U.dy - (B x W).dy vanish on a basis of H_1(O); on a trapping knot
exterior this is one condition, on a meridian. (The identification of the kernel of (B x W).dy with span(B, W) needs
B x W != 0.) Three further coupling results of spectral analysis hold at their stated scope. The curl coupling with a single-valued
pressure has an exact form in the volume coordinates of an embedding (C26, A270). On a trapping region of a
transitive hyperbolic set, periodic orbits span H_1, and under curl U = W their U-circulations test single-valued
pressure exactly (C25, A271, with a two-scale repair of the proof). A vortical regular attractor has no compact planar
cross-section of the stated type; for every straight line disjoint from it the angular derivative B.grad theta vanishes
somewhere, and for an actual profile each translated vertical-axis function F_b takes both signs (C27, A272). None of
these is a nonexistence statement for omega != 0.
Irrotational hyperbolic sets: a vortical point cannot have its backward limit inside a locally maximal hyperbolic
subset of {Omega = 0} free of zeros of B (CO14, A185, C^2; stable dimension 2 needs kappa >= d, local maximality
is used). For C-infinity profiles the conditional SRB dichotomy of item 8 sharpened this picture (on the vortical set it is now
superseded by the coverage theorem of item 1c, A308, which uses no unaudited source): there is an SRB
probability nu on the core which is either vortical (branch (V), covering (alpha*), (beta) and the vortical part of
(gamma) according to where supp nu lies) or irrotational with Omega flat on supp nu and Leb{Omega = 0} > 0
(branch (I)). Neither branch is excluded. Irrotational dynamics alone does not have zero entropy: for c = 9/20 and
one very large omega there is a harmonic polynomial phi such that B = Ay + grad phi has a compact uniformly
hyperbolic saddle set, free of zeros of B, with positive topological entropy (CO18, comparison of the second-model review
summarized in the accompanying artifacts, CONFIRMED A225). So the zero-entropy hypothesis used in A188 is not a consequence of local irrotational
structure. This extends to every c > 0 and every omega != 0 (the literature audit LIT47, PROVED, A237): a harmonic-polynomial
gradient profile with exact pressure and a compact nonsingular hyperbolic saddle horseshoe.
These examples carry no attractor and no physical measure. For every c > 0 and every omega != 0 there is also an
unbounded harmonic-gradient exact profile whose backward carrier has a compact nonsingular ergodic SRB measure with
exponents chi, 0, -3c - chi and a positive-volume basin (the literature audit LIT50, PROVED, A255, with the published Wang-Young
theorem as external input). So irrotational SRB measures are consistent with the local profile equation, and an
obstruction to branch (I) must use decay or sublinearity. None of these examples decays, is uniformly sublinear or
satisfies H1.
Mixed hyperbolic limits (synthesis CO20, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts section 20; PROVED, A267): on a transitive locally
maximal hyperbolic set of Psi without zeros of B, a C^1 transported field vanishes identically or nowhere, and a
precompact orbit whose limit set lies in a nonsingular locally maximal hyperbolic set and meets {W = 0} starts at a
zero of W (stable dimension 2 needs kappa >= div B). Hence the backward limit set of a vortical point with bounded Psi-orbit, if it lies in a locally maximal hyperbolic set free of zeros
of B, lies in {Omega != 0}. This extends CO14 from limits inside {Omega = 0} to mixed limits (case (gamma)
with alpha(a) meeting both {Omega = 0} and {Omega != 0}); it is kinematic and excludes nothing alone. The second-model review
summarized in the accompanying artifacts gives the same argument independently for regular basic hyperbolic attractors.

### B.8 Conditional and partial results (historical section 8)

Full conditional nonexistence theorems in the whole target interval, for every omega (item 1d): Theorem AX
(helicity-free, DU = O(r^(1/2)), axisymmetric actual tail; A570) and Theorem DA (helicity-free, DU = O(r^(1/2)),
and S = 0 or abs(S)^(-beta) locally integrable; A598 with A705-A708, no density premise). In the same class: the
nodal premise {k = 0} in {curl V = 0} together with a nowhere-zero tail velocity on S^2 (CO43, A730-A735), and an
empty joint core K_Omega or, around every z in K_Omega, a ball B(z, r) with S o Xi bounded on E intersect B(z, r) (LIT178, A736-A740, A1211), each give U = 0.

List from as summarized in the accompanying artifacts: H6 point-or-cycle limits (A020), period-map convergence (A011), vanishing strain plus
integrable vorticity (A029), finite energy (A031), U = o(abs(y)^(-(1-c)/c)) or U in L^p, p <= 3c/(1-c), or vorticity decay
rate > max(1/c, 2) (A053), zero entropy for smooth profiles (A055), axisymmetric U about the rotation axis (A010 after the cancellation used in A046; axisymmetric pressure gives U_theta = 0, A034), axisymmetric pressure for 0 < c < 1/2 (A3029, the literature audit LIT359, Theorem AP; at C^1, A3047, the literature audit LIT364; on one absorbing ball, A3033, the literature audit LIT360), axisymmetric pressure source tr((DU)^2) (A3040, the literature audit LIT361), one sign, a period or a return of tr((DU)^2) (A3044, the literature audit LIT362), c = 2/5 under Dini
derivative decay (A088), small rotational defect (CO8, A093, A102), zero-density vortical set (CO7, A092), c = 2/5 with bounded gradient (A103).
Omega in L^p for some 1 <= p <= 3c, or abs(Omega) = o(abs(y)^(-1/c)) (CO10, A141; p = 1 by A142); the energy criteria in
Lorentz and weighted form also exclude U in L^(p*,q), p* = 3c/(1-c), q < infinity, Omega in L^(3c,q), 1 <= q < infinity,
liminf of the weak-L^(p*) norm of U on dyadic shells equal to 0, and int_{|y|>1} |U|^2 |y|^(-(5-2/c)) < infinity
(integral-estimate analysis C19, A165-A166; for the vorticity also when the critical weak norm of exterior tails tends to 0). The
natural critical tail abs(Omega) comparable to abs(y)^(-1/c) is NOT covered by any of these criteria: it lies in
weak L^(3c), in no L^(3c,q) with q finite, and its critical integral diverges logarithmically (A169). Whether a
profile with that tail exists is OPEN. Backward limit sets contained
in {B = 0} are single points, so their basins are null (A122; the auditor proof, synthesis cross-check).
Under the A134 singular spectral hypotheses and an explicit compact trapping neighbourhood, a vortical singular
attracting set carries finitely many ergodic physical flow measures, all of entropy 1-2c (LIT30, A148).
Weak profiles (U bounded, equation in D'): with zero energy defect (for instance U Hoelder of order > 1/3)
Theorem A holds verbatim; with nonnegative defect U = 0 for c < 2/5 (integral-estimate analysis C20, A176-A177).
If Omega is tangent to every sphere centered at 0, or Omega has two global C^2 first integrals of full rank on the
vortical set, then U is constant (LIT32, A156, A157).
SRB dichotomy (CONDITIONAL on Ben Ovadia-Burguet arXiv:2506.18238v2, Theorems A, B and Claim A.1, a 2026 preprint
whose proof the team has not audited in full; implication CONFIRMED as A198, sources the literature audit LIT40, the auditor
as summarized in the accompanying artifacts, synthesis cross-check as summarized in the accompanying artifacts). Every nonconstant C-infinity
uniformly sublinear profile with 0 < c < 1/2 and any omega has a flow-ergodic SRB probability nu on its core with
exponents (chi, 0, -3c - chi), chi > 0, and either (V) nu{Omega = 0} = 0, the exponents are (1-2c, 0, -(1+c)),
the strong stable direction is the vorticity direction, the entropy is 1-2c and nu is physical; or (I)
nu{Omega = 0} = 1, Omega is flat on supp nu and {Omega = 0} has positive Lebesgue measure (possibly empty
interior). For real-analytic profiles (V) holds (A188). Proved (CO16, CONFIRMED A201): for C^2 profiles with compact trapping (H1'), Omega = 0 on
the Pesin stable manifolds of every ergodic measure carried by {Omega = 0} that gives no mass to {B = 0} and has
simple exponents (chi > 0, 0, -lambda < 0) (these hypotheses cannot be dropped from the argument, A208), and
if that measure is SRB then {Omega = 0} has positive volume, without the flatness step. This does not show that a
C^2 profile has an SRB measure, and it does not control vortical points that approach such a measure off its
stable manifolds. In branch (V) the conditional measures of nu on unstable curves have constant density with respect
to alpha-length, with plaque-dependent normalization, and holonomy along vortex lines preserves alpha-length (A207);
here time is the backward carrier time of Psi_t = Phi_{-t}, which multiplies alpha by e^{(1-2c)t} (forward B time
gives e^{-(1-2c)t}). No stable transverse invariant measure follows. Whether Lebesgue-a.e. vortical point lies in
the basin of a branch-(V) measure (the literature audit LIT41) was open; it is now PROVED in the C-infinity class without the
source (item 1c, A305-A308). The source's endpoint-compactness step (A202: bounded C^r curves need not be
precompact in C^(r-1,1)) remains a qualification of the CONDITIONAL dichotomy above, which the vortical set no
longer needs. For a regular attractor
the SRB measure defines a closed unstable current T(beta) = int beta(Z) dnu, alpha(Z) = 1, with boundary identity
and int U.Z dnu = 1/(1-2c) (synthesis section 18, A217); these identities give no contradiction.
Far field (integral-estimate analysis C23, C24). Under H0, Hb and the Dini condition, for 2/5 < c < 3/5 and every omega, the remainder
W = U - U~ after the scattering tail U~ is in L^2, and (5c-2) norm(W)_2^2 = 2N, where N = int U (x) U : grad U~
converges absolutely and N > 0 if U != 0 (CONDITIONAL, A250). If instead the Lamb vector Omega x U is in L^p for one
1 < p < p* = 3c/(1-c) (sufficient: a natural annular L^p bound on Omega), then U = V + W with V exactly twisted
homogeneous of degree -(1-c)/c, W in L^p, and exponential convergence of the twisted blow-down (CONDITIONAL, A251).
Adjoint moments (integral-estimate analysis C25, PROVED at this scope, A254): for 2/5 < c < 1/2, every omega, under H0 with U in C^1 and Hb,
the quadratic moment int U (x) U : grad Phi converges absolutely and is a limit of shell averages for every Phi in the
infinite-dimensional kernel K* of the adjoint tail operator, {div Phi = 0, (1-4c)Phi - omega J Phi - (Ay.grad)Phi = 0};
under the A251 hypothesis or Dini it equals c times the pairing of the tail profile with the angular part of Phi. For the
rotation field Phi = abs(y)^(k-4) J y, k = (1-c)/c, it is (k-4) int abs(y)^(k-6) (U.Jy)(U.y). The toroidal elements
determine the radial vorticity of the tail. For every nonzero tail there is a smooth adjoint test with strictly
positive moment (integral-estimate analysis T9.4, A281), so these identities are compatible with nonzero tails.
No sign contradiction is derived from any of these.
Finite-regularity coverage and Liouville theorem (CONDITIONAL, A416-A417, A422): for 0 < c < 1/2, every omega and
C^r uniformly sublinear profiles with integer r >= 2, the bound Gamma_Z < r(1-2c) gives the coverage of item 1c(i).
For decaying profiles with P in C^1 and 2/5 <= c < 1/2, one sign of U.Omega on each D_nu then forces U = 0. The bound
is a profile-dependent hypothesis of type H6 and is not known to follow from decay (A417). The bound may be replaced
by the weaker componentwise bounds Gamma_E < r(1-2c), one for each component E of {Omega != 0} (A430-A432; item 1c).
Coverage for C^r, r >= 3,
also follows from the strain bound (r-1)(1-2c) > L_+ + L_- (CONDITIONAL, A312, A373).
Constant reduced Bernoulli function (the literature audit LIT51, CONDITIONAL theorem, A256): for 0 < c < 1/2, every omega, H0 with
U in C^2 and U uniformly sublinear, if H = P + abs(U)^2/2 + (Ay).U is spatially constant then U = 0. Constancy of H is a
hypothesis; it is not derived from decay. Localizations (the literature audit LIT55, LIT56, CONDITIONAL theorems, A265-A266, every
0 < c < 1/2 and every omega): under uniform sublinearity, grad H = 0 on the open vortical set {Omega != 0} already makes
U constant (zero under decay); under decay it suffices that open sets on which H is constant, with possibly different
constants, cover almost every vortical point. Constancy on a single basin that is not dense is open.
Helicity-free regular basins (synthesis CO21, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts section 21, CONDITIONAL theorem, A268; with the literature audit
LIT58, A273): for every 0 < c < 1/2 and every omega, if U -> 0, almost every vortical point lies in the basin of a
regular backward attractor of CO9, U.Omega = 0 on these basins, and in each such attractor A every strong stable set
W^ss(x) meet A is dense in A, then U = 0. The proof: Omega.grad H = -(1-2c) U.Omega makes H constant on vortex lines,
density of the strong stable sets makes it constant on each basin, and LIT55 (A265) concludes. The density hypothesis
holds when A is topologically mixing: every strong stable set is dense in a compact nonsingular locally maximal mixing
hyperbolic flow set (LIT58, A273). It fails for a constant return time (constant roof), where H is only a function of
the phase. A variant (the literature audit LIT57, A269, C^3) replaces strong stable density by a global rank argument under a dense
vortical set, global zero helicity and separately stated SRB density and coverage premises. Coverage, zero helicity
and mixing are hypotheses; none is derived from decay. So case (alpha*) is excluded under these H9-type hypotheses;
mixing is not needed (next paragraph); nonzero helicity density of both signs is open.
Without mixing (the literature audit LIT59, CONDITIONAL theorem, A277-A278): for decaying C^2 profiles, 2/5 <= c < 1/2 and every
omega, one pressure constant gives a reduced Bernoulli function H0 = H - const with int_{B_R} H0^2 <= C R^(7-2/c) and
int_Q H0(Phi_t)^2 <= C_Q exp(-2(1-2c)t) for bounded Q; if U.Omega = 0 on the essential basin of a given vortical SRB
measure with positive unstable conditional densities, then H0 = 0 there, and almost-everywhere coverage of the
vortical set by such basins gives U = 0. Mixing, a dense vortical set and C^3 are not used. One sign suffices
(the literature audit LIT60, A283): for C^2 uniformly sublinear profiles, 0 < c < 1/2, every omega, helicity of one sign on an open
forward-vortex-invariant set vanishes there, and a two-sided recurrent orbit through a point with U.Omega != 0 meets
both signs arbitrarily far in both time directions. So the helicity premise of CO21, LIT58 and LIT59 can be weakened
to one sign on each basin. In the C-infinity class the existence of the measures and the coverage of the
vortical set are now PROVED (A308), and the combination is the Liouville theorem of item 1c (A309). Sign-changing
helicity remains open.
For the regular attractors of CO9 no SRB measure is needed (synthesis CO22, as summarized in the accompanying artifacts section 23,
CONDITIONAL theorem, A290-A291, every 0 < c < 1/2 and every omega, under Hb: U bounded and U(R.) -> 0 in D'). A
periodic orbit of the attractor makes H periodic in B-time on the basin, so U.B = -(B.grad H)/(1-2c) is invariant
